sentences.zh: 皇甫謐

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐，字士安，幼名靜，安定朝那人，漢太尉嵩之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi, courtesy name Shi'an, childhood name Jing, was a man of Chaona in Anding, great-grandson of the Han Grand Commandant Song.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi, courtesy name Shi'an, childhood name Jing, came from Chaona in Anding. He was the great-grandson of Grand Commandant Huangfu Song of Han.

sentences.zh: 出叔父，徙居新安。

translations.literal: He went out to his uncle and moved residence to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was given to an uncle for adoption and moved to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 年二十，不好學，遊蕩無度，或以為癡。

translations.literal: At twenty he did not love learning; he roamed and wandered without measure—some thought him dull.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he still spurned study for idle roaming—people took him for simple.

sentences.zh: 嘗得瓜果，輒進所叔母任氏。

translations.literal: Once when he obtained melons and fruits he always presented them to his aunt by adoption, Lady Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had fruit, he offered it first to his foster aunt, Lady Ren.

sentences.zh: 任氏曰：「《孝經》云：『三牲之養，猶為不孝。

translations.literal: Lady Ren said, "The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Even offering the three sacrificial beasts counts as unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ren told him: "The Classic of Filial Piety warns that even feeding parents the three sacrificial meats can still be unfilial."

sentences.zh: 』汝今年餘二十，目不存教，心不入道，無以慰我。

translations.literal: 'You are already past twenty; your eyes hold no teaching; your heart does not enter the Way—there is nothing to console me.
translations.idiomatic: You are past twenty yet refuse instruction and ignore the Way—you bring me no comfort."

sentences.zh: 」因歎曰：「昔孟母三徙以成仁，曾父烹豕以存教，豈我居不卜鄰，教有所闕，何爾魯鈍之甚也！

translations.literal: " She sighed and said, "Formerly Mother Meng thrice moved to complete benevolence; Zeng's father cooked a pig to preserve teaching—could it be I did not choose neighbors well and my teaching has gaps—why are you so dull!
translations.idiomatic: She sighed: "The mothers of Mencius and Zengzi bent heaven and earth to rear their sons—have I failed to choose good neighbors or left gaps in your schooling? How can you be so thick-headed!"

sentences.zh: 修身篤學，自汝得之，于我何有！

translations.literal: Cultivate the body and devote yourself to learning—you obtain it yourself—what have I to do with it!
translations.idiomatic: Master yourself and study—that achievement is yours alone, not mine!"

sentences.zh: 」因對之流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: With that she wept before him.

sentences.zh: 謐乃感激，就鄉人席坦受書，勤力不怠。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon was moved; he went to fellow townsman Xi Tan to receive books—diligent without slack.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred to remorse, he studied under Xi Tan of his village without slackening.

sentences.zh: 居貧，躬自稼穡，帶經而農，遂博綜典籍百家之言。

translations.literal: Dwelling poor, he personally plowed and harvested; he belted his classics while farming—thereupon broadly synthesized canonical texts and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor he farmed his own fields, classics tucked in his belt, until he commanded every major text and school.

sentences.zh: 沈靜寡欲，始有高尚之志，以著述為務，自號玄晏先生。

translations.literal: Deep and quiet, few desires—he began to have lofty aims; he took writing as task; styled himself Master Xuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn and detached, he aspired high and devoted himself to authorship, calling himself Master Xuanyan.

sentences.zh: 著《禮樂》、《聖真》之論。

translations.literal: He composed treatises on ritual and music and on sagehood and truth.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote essays on ritual and music and on sagehood and authenticity.

sentences.zh: 後得風痹疾，猶手不輟卷。

translations.literal: Later he contracted wind-numbness illness—yet his hand did not lay aside scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Even after crippling wind-numbness struck, he never put down his books.

sentences.zh: 或勸謐修名廣交，謐以為「非聖人孰能兼存出處，居田里之中亦可以樂堯、舜之道，何必崇接世利，事官鞅掌，然後為名乎」。

translations.literal: Some urged Mi to cultivate fame and widen friendships; Mi held that "unless a sage who can jointly preserve exiting and entering—in dwelling in fields and hamlets one also can enjoy Yao and Shun's Way—why must one honor worldly profit, serve office busily grasping, and only then be famed?".
translations.idiomatic: When urged to network for renown he replied: "Only sages balance retirement and service; one may savor Yao and Shun even in a village—why chase profit and harness office before claiming fame?"

sentences.zh: 作《玄守論》以答之，曰：

translations.literal: He composed the "Discourse on Guarding the Dark" to answer them, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He answered with his "Discourse on Guarding the Dark" in these terms:

sentences.zh: 遂不仕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore refused office.

sentences.zh: 耽玩典籍，忘寢與食，時人謂之「書淫」。

translations.literal: He indulged in classics, forgetting sleep and food—people of the time called him the "book debauchee.".
translations.idiomatic: He buried himself in texts until he forgot meals and sleep—contemporaries dubbed him a "book debauchee."

sentences.zh: 或有箴其過篤，將損耗精神。

translations.literal: Some admonished him for excess devotion—it would waste spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Well-wishers warned that such zeal would ruin his health.

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣，況命之修短分定懸天乎！」

translations.literal: Mi said: "Hear the Way at dawn—die at dusk content—how much more fate's length and shortness are allotted and hang from Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If I grasp the Way at dawn I may die at dusk content—why fret when Heaven fixes life's span?"

sentences.zh: 叔父有子既冠，謐年四十喪所生後母，遂還本宗。

translations.literal: His uncle had a son already capped; Mi at forty mourned his birth mother who had become stepmother—thereupon returned to his original lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Once his cousin came of age and Mi turned forty, he buried the mother who bore him and then rejoined his birth clan.

sentences.zh: 城陽太守梁柳，謐從姑子也，當之官，人勸謐餞之。

translations.literal: Liu Liu, governor of Chengyang—Mi's aunt's son—was about to take office; people urged Mi to host a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Liu of Chengyang—his aunt's son—was leaving for his post; friends urged Huangfu Mi to give him a send-off banquet.

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「柳為布衣時過吾，吾送迎不出門，食不過鹽菜，貧者不以酒肉為禮。

translations.literal: Mi said: "When Liu was common cloth visiting me I did not see him beyond the gate and meals were only pickles—the poor do not use wine and meat as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi refused: "When Liang Liu was a commoner I never stepped beyond my gate to greet him and meals never rose above pickles—poverty forbids wine-laden etiquette."

sentences.zh: 今作郡而送之，是貴城陽太守而賤梁柳，豈中古人之道，是非吾心所安也。」

translations.literal: Now he becomes governor and I send him off—that esteems the governor of Chengyang and despises Liang Liu—how does that hit ancient men's Way—it is not what my heart rests in."
translations.idiomatic: To banquet him now as governor would honor the office and insult the man—hardly the ancient code, and not what my conscience allows."

sentences.zh: 時魏郡召上計掾，舉孝廉；

translations.literal: At the time Wei commandery summoned him as accounting clerk; he was recommended Filial and Incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: Wei commandery nominated him accounting clerk and Filial and Incorrupt;

sentences.zh: 景元初，相國辟，皆不行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingyuan era the minister of state summoned him—he did none.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyuan the minister of state summoned him—he declined each.

sentences.zh: 其後鄉親勸令應命，謐為《釋勸論》以通志焉。

translations.literal: Afterward fellow villagers urged him to obey orders; Mi composed the "Discourse Releasing Persuasion" to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When kin pressed him to answer summons he wrote the "Discourse Releasing Persuasion" to clarify his resolve.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：其後武帝頻下詔敦逼不已，謐上疏自稱草莽臣曰：「臣以尪弊，迷於道趣，因疾抽簪，散發林阜，人綱不閑，鳥獸為群。

translations.literal: Its words say: Afterward Emperor Wu repeatedly issued edicts urging without cease; Mi submitted memorial styling himself commoner minister, saying: "Your servant by frail weakness is lost in the Way's ends; because of illness plucked his hairpin, scattered hair in woods and hills—human ties unskilled, birds and beasts as companions.
translations.idiomatic: The scrap begins "Thus he spoke," yet the chapter immediately jumps to Emperor Wu's repeated summons; Huangfu Mi memorialized as a recluse: "I am frail and obsessed with private aims; illness drove me to cast aside office and herd with beasts in the hills, ignorant of courtly ties."

sentences.zh: 陛下披榛采蘭，並收蒿艾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty parts brambles to gather orchids—and also gathers mugwort and wormwood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty winnows fine orchids from the scrub—and still gathers mugwort with them."

sentences.zh: 是以皋陶振褐，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Therefore Gao Yao shook his coarse cloak—the unkind departed far.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Gao Yao left his hut and the cruel fled."

sentences.zh: 臣惟頑蒙，備食晉粟，猶識唐人擊壤之樂，宜赴京城，稱壽闕外。

translations.literal: Your servant alone is stubbornly ignorant—yet feeds on Jin grain—still knows the Tang people's joy of beating clods—ought to hurry to the capital and toast longevity outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Though dull I eat Jin grain and still recall the Tang villagers' contentment—I should kneel at the capital and shout long life."

sentences.zh: 而小人無良，致災速禍，久嬰篤疾，軀半不仁，右腳偏小，十有九載。

translations.literal: Yet petty men lack good faith—bringing disaster swiftly—long pressed by grave illness—half the body without feeling—the right foot somewhat small—for nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: But I am none too good; sickness struck fast—nine years half-paralyzed, my right foot shrunken."

sentences.zh: 又服寒食藥，違錯節度，辛苦荼毒，於今七年。

translations.literal: Moreover I took Cold Food Powder—mistook dosage—bitter poison—for seven years now.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food Powder misused has poisoned me seven years."

sentences.zh: 隆冬裸袒食冰，當暑煩悶，加以咳逆，或若溫虐，或類傷寒，浮氣流腫，四肢酸重。

translations.literal: In deepest winter naked eating ice—in heat vexed and stifling—plus coughing fits—sometimes like warm malaria—sometimes like cold injury—floating qi flowing swelling—four limbs sore heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Winters I shiver naked gnawing ice; summers I suffocate with coughs—now malaria-like, now chill-like—edema and aching limbs."

sentences.zh: 於今困劣，救命呼噏，父兄見出，妻息長訣。

translations.literal: Now trapped and weak—calling for breath to save life—father and brothers see me off—wife and children long farewell.
translations.idiomatic: I am too weak to breathe; kin escort me while I bid wife and children forever."

sentences.zh: 仰迫天威，扶輿就道，所苦加焉，不任進路，委身待罪，伏枕歎息。

translations.literal: Looking up pressed by heavenly awe—supported in litter taking road—what I suffer adds—I cannot bear advancing on the road—entrust body awaiting crime—lean on pillow sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's command forces me into a litter though each league worsens my pain—I lie waiting judgment, sighing on my pillow."

sentences.zh: 臣聞《韶》《衛》不並奏，《雅》《鄭》不兼禦，故郤子入周，禍延王叔；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard 'Shao' and 'Wei' are not played together—'Elegant' and 'Zheng' are not both driven—therefore when Xi Ke entered Zhou disaster extended to Prince Shu;
translations.idiomatic: I know Shao and Wei music never mix; when Xi Ke entered Zhou the king suffered."

sentences.zh: 虞丘稱賢，樊姬掩口。

translations.literal: Yu Qiu praised worthiness—Lady Fan covered her mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qiu's praise made Lady Fan of Chu hide a smile."

sentences.zh: 君子小人，禮不同器，況臣糠䵃，糅之彫胡？

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man—ritual uses different vessels—how much more your servant chaff and husks—mix them with polished grain?
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and commoners do not share vessels—how dare chaff like me mix with polished rice?"

sentences.zh: 庸夫錦衣，不稱其服也。

translations.literal: A vulgar husband in brocade robes—does not match his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Silk on a peasant never fits."

sentences.zh: 竊聞同命之士，咸以畢到，唯臣疾疢，抱釁床蓐，雖貪明時，懼斃命路隅。

translations.literal: Privately hearing fellow summoned scholars all have arrived—only your servant ill—embracing illness on bed mat—although greedy for bright times—fears dying at road's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Others summoned have arrived; only I lie sick in bed—though I crave this enlightened reign I might die on the road."

sentences.zh: 設臣不疾，已遭堯、舜之世，執志箕山，猶當容之。

translations.literal: Suppose your servant were not ill—already encountering Yao and Shun's age—holding resolve at Mount Ji—still ought tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Even hale in Yao-Shun days I would hide on Mount Ji—surely allowed."

sentences.zh: 臣聞上有明聖之主，下有輸實之臣；

translations.literal: Your servant hears above there is bright sage lord—below there is conveying substance ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When the throne is wise ministers prove earnest;"

sentences.zh: 上有在寬之政，下有委情之人。

translations.literal: Above there is lenient governance—below there are men who entrust feeling.
translations.idiomatic: when policy is generous subjects give their hearts."

sentences.zh: 唯陛下留神垂恕，更旌瑰俊，索隱于傅岩，收釣於渭濱，無令泥滓久濁清流。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty attend spirit and drop forgiveness—again signal splendid talents—seek hidden at Fu Rock—gather fishing at Wei bank—do not let mud long muddy clear stream.
translations.idiomatic: Please look kindly elsewhere—seek Fu Yue and Jiang Taigong—and keep mud from fouling clear water."

sentences.zh: 」謐辭切言至，遂見聽許。

translations.literal: " Mi's words cut utmost speech arrived—thereupon was heard and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi spoke so earnestly that the emperor let him be.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，又舉賢良方正，並不起。

translations.literal: After more than a year again raised Worthy, Good and Upright—together did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was nominated Worthy, Good, and Upright—again he stayed home.

sentences.zh: 自表就帝借書，帝送一車書與之。

translations.literal: He personally memorialized to borrow books from the emperor—the emperor sent one cart of books to him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to borrow imperial books; the emperor sent a whole cart.

sentences.zh: 謐雖羸疾，而披閱不怠。

translations.literal: Although Mi was emaciated ill—yet reading did not slack.
translations.idiomatic: Gaunt as he was, he never stopped reading.

sentences.zh: 初服寒食散，而性與之忤，每委頓不倫，嘗悲恚，叩刃欲自殺，叔母諫之而止。

translations.literal: First taking Cold Food Powder—yet nature contradicted it—each time collapsed beyond measure—once bitterly angry drew blade wishing suicide—aunt remonstrated and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food Powder disagreed with him—fits left him wrecked; once he seized a knife until his aunt stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 濟陰太守蜀人文立，表以命士有贄為煩，請絕其禮幣，詔從之。

translations.literal: Governor of Jiyin Wen Li from Shu memorialized that nominated gentlemen found presents burdensome—requested cut off ritual silk—edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li of Shu, governor of Jiyin, asked to end congratulatory gifts for nominees—the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 謐聞而歎曰：「亡國之大夫不可與圖存，而以革歷代之制，其可乎！

translations.literal: Mi heard and sighed: "A conquered state's grandees cannot plot survival—yet want change dynastic institutions—can it be!
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi groaned: "Can ministers of a fallen state remake eternal rites?"

sentences.zh: 夫『束帛戔戔』，《易》之明義，玄纁之贄，自古之舊也。

translations.literal: The bundle of silk modest—the Changes makes bright meaning—dark-red tribute—from antiquity's old.
translations.idiomatic: "Bolts of silk" mark clear meaning in the Changes—dark silk gifts are ancient usage."

sentences.zh: 故孔子稱夙夜強學以待問，席上之珍以待聘。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius praised studying hard day and night awaiting questions—treasures on mats awaiting summons.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius prized scholars who refine themselves for audience and keep treasures for patrons."

sentences.zh: 士於是乎三揖乃進，明致之難也；

translations.literal: The gentleman then thrice bows before advancing—manifesting arrival's difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: Three bows show how hard it is to advance;"

sentences.zh: 一讓而退，明去之易也。

translations.literal: once yielding then withdrawing—manifesting departure's ease.
translations.idiomatic: one yielding shows how easy it is to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 若殷湯之于伊尹，文王之于太公，或身即莘野，或就載以歸，唯恐禮之不重，豈吝其煩費哉！

translations.literal: Like Yin Tang toward Yi Yin—King Wen toward Grand Duke—sometimes personally at Shen wilds—sometimes riding carriage returning—only feared ritual not heavy—how stingy trouble expense!
translations.idiomatic: Tang sought Yi Yin and Wen sought Taigong in the weeds—never minding cost—lest courtesy fall short."

sentences.zh: 且一禮不備，貞女恥之，況命士乎！

translations.literal: Moreover one ritual incomplete—a chaste maiden shames it—how much more a commissioned gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: One lapse shames a maiden—how much more a sworn scholar!"

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『賜也，爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Ci—you love the sheep—I love the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius told Zigong: you spare the sheep—I defend the rite."

sentences.zh: 』棄之如何？

translations.literal: 'Abandon it—how?
translations.idiomatic: Drop it—what then?"

sentences.zh: 政之失賢，於此乎在矣。」

translations.literal: Government's losing worthies—is here it lies."
translations.idiomatic: When government loses worthy men this is where it begins."

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，又詔曰：「男子皇甫謐沈靜履素，守學好古，與流俗異趣，其以謐為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning again edict said: "The man Huangfu Mi is deep quiet treading plain—guards learning loves antiquity—with vulgar currents different bent—let Mi be attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning an edict praised Huangfu Mi's purity and love of antiquity and named him attendant to the heir.

sentences.zh: 」謐固辭篤疾。

translations.literal: " Mi firmly declined grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded grave illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 帝初雖不奪其志，尋復發詔徵為議郎，又召補著作郎。

translations.literal: The emperor at first although did not seize his intent—soon again issued edict summon as counselor—again summoned supplement Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor first indulged him he soon summoned him counselor and compiler.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉劉毅請為功曹，並不應。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Liu Yi requested him as merit clerk—together did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan governor Liu Yi sought him as merit clerk—still no answer.

sentences.zh: 著論為葬送之制，名曰《篤終》，曰：而竟不仕。

translations.literal: He composed treatise on burial sending system—named 'Dying with Resolve'—saying: yet in end did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted burial regulations titled "Dying with Resolve"; nevertheless he never took office.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年六十八。

translations.literal: He died—age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子童靈、方回等遵其遺命。

translations.literal: Sons Tongling, Fanghui and others followed his dying orders.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Tongling and Fanghui honored his last wishes.

sentences.zh: 謐所著詩賦誄頌論難甚多，又撰《帝王世紀》、《年曆》、《高士》、《逸士》、《列女》等傳、《玄晏春秋》，並重於世。

translations.literal: Mi's composed poems, rhapsodies, dirges, hymns, treatises, challenges very many—also compiled Records of August Ages, chronologies, biographies of lofty recluses and reclusive women, Xuanyan Annals—all weighted in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left vast poetry and prose plus Records of August Ages, chronologies, collections of recluses and exemplary women, and the Xuanyan Annals—all esteemed.

sentences.zh: 門人摯虞、張軌、牛綜、席純，皆為晉名臣。

translations.literal: Disciples Zhi Yu, Zhang Gui, Niu Zong, Xi Chun—all became Jin famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Students Zhi Yu, Zhang Gui, Niu Zong, and Xi Chun rose to Jin ministerial rank.

translations.literal: The edition inserts a ruled line before the subsection on the son.
translations.idiomatic: The layout marks the turn to his son.

sentences.zh: 子方回

translations.literal: Son Fanghui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huangfu Fanghui

sentences.zh: =方回少遵父操，兼有文才。

translations.literal: Fanghui in youth followed father's conduct—also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Fanghui kept his father's discipline and showed literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，博士征，不起。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia erudite summoned—did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia opened he ignored summons to the erudite academy.

sentences.zh: 避亂荊州，閉戶閒居，未嘗入城府。

translations.literal: Fleeing chaos to Jingzhou—closed door idle dwelling—never entered prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: He fled turmoil to Jingzhou, shut his gate, and never entered the yamen.

sentences.zh: 蠶而後衣，耕而後食，先人後己，尊賢愛物，南土人士咸崇敬之。

translations.literal: Only after silkworms then clothed—only after plowing then ate—others first self later—honored worthies cherished creatures—southern gentlemen all revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He wore silk only after raising silkworms and ate after harvest—others before himself—and southland scholars revered him.

sentences.zh: 刺史陶侃禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: Inspector Tao Kan treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Kan honored him richly.

sentences.zh: 侃每造之，著素士服，望門輒下而進。

translations.literal: Kan each time visited him—wearing plain scholar robes—seeing gate then dismounted and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan always wore plain clothes and dismounted before Fanghui's gate.

sentences.zh: 王敦遣從弟暠代侃，遷侃為廣州。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent cousin Hao replace Kan—transferred Kan to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun replaced Tao Kan with cousin Wang Hao and moved Kan to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侃將詣敦，方回諫曰：「吾聞敵國滅，功臣亡。

translations.literal: Kan was about to visit Dun—Fanghui remonstrated: "I hear when enemy states perish merit ministers die.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan planned to visit Wang Dun, Fanghui warned: conquerors soon kill their champions."

sentences.zh: 足下新破杜弢，功莫與二，欲無危，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Underfoot you newly broke Du Tao—merit none compares second—wish no danger—how can obtain!
translations.idiomatic: You just crushed Du Tao unmatched—how can you stay safe?"

sentences.zh: 」侃不從而行。

translations.literal: " Kan did not follow but went.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan went anyway.

sentences.zh: 敦果欲殺侃，賴周訪獲免。

translations.literal: Dun indeed wished kill Kan—relied on Zhou Fang obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun nearly executed him—Zhou Fang saved him.

sentences.zh: 暠既至荊州，大失物情，百姓叛暠迎杜弢。

translations.literal: After Hao arrived Jingzhou—greatly lost people's sentiment—commoners rebelled Hao welcoming Du Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao alienated Jingzhou until commoners welcomed Du Tao back.

sentences.zh: 暠大行誅戮以立威，以方回為侃所敬，責其不來詣己，乃收而斬之。

translations.literal: Hao greatly carried out executions slaughter to establish awe—because Fanghui was whom Kan respected—blamed him for not coming visit himself—thereupon seized and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao slaughtered widely for terror; resenting Fanghui's prestige with Tao Kan, he arrested and executed him.

sentences.zh: 荊土華夷，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Chinese and barbarians—none did not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and natives of Jing wept together.

sentences.zh: 摯虞

translations.literal: Zhi Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu

sentences.zh: 摯虞，字仲洽，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, courtesy name Zhongqia—capital district Chang'an man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, courtesy name Zhongqia, came from Chang'an in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 父模，魏太僕卿。

translations.literal: Father Mo—Wei Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi Mo served Wei as Minister Coachman.

sentences.zh: 虞少事皇甫謐，才學通博，著述不倦。

translations.literal: Yu in youth studied under Huangfu Mi—talent learning broadly penetrating—writing without fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Youth study under Huangfu Mi gave him encyclopedic learning and tireless authorship.

sentences.zh: 郡檄主簿。

translations.literal: Commandery summoned chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery drafted him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 虞嘗以死生有命，富貴在天。

translations.literal: Yu once held death and life have fate—wealth and honor rest with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He held that life and death are fated and wealth heaven-sent.

sentences.zh: 天之所祐者義也，人之所助者信也。

translations.literal: What Heaven blesses is righteousness—what men assist is trust.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven favors the dutiful; men help the trustworthy."

sentences.zh: 履信思順，所以延福，違此而行，所以速禍。

translations.literal: Treading trust thinking compliance—thereby extends fortune—violating this and acting—thereby hastens disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Faith and docility prolong fortune; defiance hastens ruin."

sentences.zh: 然道長世短，禍福舛錯，怵迫之徒，不知所守，蕩而積憤，或迷或放。

translations.literal: Yet Way long world short—fortune misfortune crisscross—frightened pressed persons—do not know what they guard—dissolute yet accumulating rage—sometimes lost sometimes unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet life is brief and fate tangled—anxious souls lose anchor and drift or rage."

sentences.zh: 故借之以身，假之以事，先陳處世不遇之難，遂棄彝倫，輕舉遠遊，以極常人罔惑之情，而後引之以正，反之以義，推神明之應於視聽之表，崇否泰之運于智力之外，以明天任命之不可違，故作《思遊賦》。

translations.literal: Therefore borrowing by body—lending by affairs—first lay out dwelling in age unmet difficulty—thereupon abandon constant relations—lightly rise far roam—to exhaust common men's net confusion feeling—afterward lead them by rectitude—return them by righteousness—extend spirit illumination's responses beyond sight and hearing—elevate fortune's turning beyond intellect—thereby clarify Heaven bright mandate cannot be disobeyed—therefore composed 'Rhapsody on Pondering Roaming.'
translations.idiomatic: So he framed the "Rhapsody on Pondering Roaming": feign exile and wandering to mirror mortal confusion, then guide readers back to duty, proving Heaven's decree beyond wit.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：舉賢良，與夏侯湛等十七人策為下第，拜中郎。

translations.literal: Its words say: Raised Worthy and Good—together with Xia Hou Zhan etc. seventeen persons examined ranked lowest rank—appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The opening "Thus he spoke" collides with office history: nominated Worthy and Good with Xia Hou Zhan and sixteen others he scored lowest yet became gentleman cadet.

sentences.zh: 武帝詔曰：「省諸賢良答策，雖所言殊塗，皆明于王義，有益政道。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu edict said: "Having examined various Worthy and Good answer examinations—although what they spoke divergent paths—all illumined kingly righteousness—benefit governance Way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replied: "Though answers differed, each clarified royal doctrine for governance."

sentences.zh: 欲詳覽其對，究觀賢士大夫用心。

translations.literal: Wish to examine in detail their responses—thoroughly observe worthy scholar-officials' intentions.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to study each answer and weigh scholars' intent.

sentences.zh: 」因詔諸賢良方正直言，會東堂策問，曰：「頃日食正陽，水旱為災，將何所修，以變大眚？

translations.literal: Thereupon he commanded those recommended as worthy, upright, and outspoken to assemble in the Eastern Hall for policy questions, saying: "Recently the sun was eclipsed at noon, and floods and droughts have become disasters—what must we cultivate and set right in order to transform this great calamity?"
translations.idiomatic: He therefore summoned all candidates rated worthy, upright, and candid to gather in the Eastern Hall for the examination and asked: "Of late the sun was darkened at midday, and flood and drought have struck. What should we reform to turn aside this great scourge?"

sentences.zh: 及法令有不宜於今，為公私所患苦者，皆何事？

translations.literal: As for laws and regulations that are unsuitable for the present and are a source of hardship to both the public and private spheres—what are all these things?"
translations.idiomatic: What statutes ill suit our age and vex both the state and the people?"

sentences.zh: 凡平世在於得才，得才者亦借耳目以聽察。

translations.literal: In general, peace in the age lies in obtaining talent; those who obtain talent likewise borrow ears and eyes to listen and observe."
translations.idiomatic: Ordering the realm rests on winning good men, and winning good men depends on opening one's ears and eyes to what is heard and seen."

sentences.zh: 若有文武器能有益於時務而未見申敘者，各舉其人。

translations.literal: If there are those whose civil and military talents would benefit current affairs yet have not been recommended and described, each should nominate such persons."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone possesses civil or military gifts that would serve the times but has not yet been properly recommended, each of you should put that person forward."

sentences.zh: 及有負俗謗議，宜先洗濯者，亦各言之。

translations.literal: And as for those burdened by vulgar reproach and slander who ought first to be cleared, each should likewise speak of them."
translations.idiomatic: And if there are men weighed down by popular scandal who deserve to be vindicated first, speak for them as well."

sentences.zh: 」虞對曰：「臣聞古之聖明，原始以要終，體本以正末。

translations.literal: " Yu replied: "Your servant has heard that the sage rulers of antiquity traced the beginning to grasp the end and embraced the root to rectify the branches."
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered: "I have heard that the sage kings of old searched origins to understand outcomes and held fast to the root to set the branches straight."

sentences.zh: 故憂法度之不當，而不憂人物之失所；

translations.literal: Therefore they worried that laws and norms were inappropriate, and did not worry that men had lost their proper places;
translations.idiomatic: They therefore fretted first when institutions went awry, not merely when individuals were misplaced;

sentences.zh: 憂人物之失所，而不憂災害之流行。

translations.literal: they worried that men had lost their proper places, and did not worry that disasters were spreading."
translations.idiomatic: they cared when talent was misassigned before they blamed Heaven for calamities."

sentences.zh: 誠以法得於此，則物理於彼；

translations.literal: Truly, because when principle is secured here, affairs are ordered there;
translations.idiomatic: For when right rule holds here, order follows there;

sentences.zh: 人和於下，則災消於上。

translations.literal: when the people are harmonious below, disasters dissolve above."
translations.idiomatic: when the folk live in harmony below, calamities cease above."

sentences.zh: 其有日月之眚，水旱之災，則反聽內視，求其所由，遠觀諸物，近驗諸身。

translations.literal: Whenever there were faults of sun and moon or disasters of flood and drought, they turned listening inward and looked within themselves, sought the causes thereof, surveyed distant phenomena, and verified what was near in their own persons."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever eclipses appeared or floods and droughts struck, they listened inwardly, examined themselves, traced origins, observed things afar, and tested truth at hand."

sentences.zh: 耳目聽察，豈或有蔽其聰明者乎？

translations.literal: In listening and observing with ears and eyes—could anything be obscuring their clarity?"
translations.idiomatic: Could anything be clouding clear perception in what we hear and see?"

sentences.zh: 動心出令，豈或有傾其常正者乎？

translations.literal: In moving the heart and issuing orders—could anything be overturning their constant rectitude?"
translations.idiomatic: Could anything be upsetting steadiness and justice in our intentions and edicts?"

sentences.zh: 大官大職，豈或有授非其人者乎？

translations.literal: In great offices and great posts—could there be appointments of those who are not the right men?"
translations.idiomatic: Could any high office have gone to the wrong person?"

sentences.zh: 賞罰黜陟，豈或有不得其所者乎？

translations.literal: In rewards, punishments, dismissals, and promotions—could there be cases where they did not reach their proper targets?"
translations.idiomatic: Could rewards and penalties, promotions and demotions, ever miss their mark?"

sentences.zh: 河濱山岩，豈或有懷道釣築而未感於夢兆者乎？

translations.literal: By riverbanks and mountain cliffs—could there be those who cherish the Way, fishing and quarrying stone, who have not been touched by auspicious dreams?"
translations.idiomatic: Along rivers and in mountain retreats, might gifted men still hidden—like those who fished or hewed stone—have failed to appear even in portents?"

sentences.zh: 方外遐裔，豈或有命世傑出而未蒙膏澤者乎？

translations.literal: Beyond the frontiers, in distant tribes—could there be those outstanding enough to order the age who have not received moistening grace?"
translations.idiomatic: In the farthest corners of the realm, might brilliant men who could define their generation still lack the dew of royal favor?"

sentences.zh: 推此類也，以求其故，詢事考言，以盡其實，則天人之情可得而見，咎征之至可得而救也。

translations.literal: Extending cases of this kind to seek their causes, inquiring into affairs and examining words so as to exhaust the reality—then the sentiments of Heaven and man can be discerned, and the onset of reproving omens can be remedied."
translations.idiomatic: Press such inquiries to learn why things happen; weigh deeds and words until the truth is plain—then the bond between Heaven and humanity becomes visible, and threatening signs can be answered."

sentences.zh: 若推之於物則無忤，求之於身則無尤，萬物理順，內外咸宜，祝史正辭，言不負誠，而日月錯行，夭癘不戒，此則陰陽之事，非吉凶所在也。

translations.literal: If, when extended to things, there is no violation, and when sought in oneself there is no fault—if the myriad things are ordered smoothly and inner and outer are all fitting, and invokers and scribes use correct phrases so that words do not betray sincerity—yet sun and moon run awry and untimely death and pestilence offer no warning—this is a matter of yin and yang, not where fortune and misfortune reside."
translations.idiomatic: If the realm answers scrutiny without contradiction and the ruler's conscience is clear—if all runs smoothly within and without and ritual language stays honest—yet the luminaries wander and plague strikes without warning, that belongs to cosmic imbalance, not to moral reward or blame."

sentences.zh: 期運度數，自然之分，固非人事所能供禦，其亦振廩散滯，貶食省用而已矣。

translations.literal: The reckonings of destined cycles and natural allotment are indeed not what human affairs can supply or ward off; at most one shakes open the granaries, disperses stagnation, reduces meals, and cuts expenditures—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The turning of fate and the count of nature lie beyond human power; we can only open the granaries, ease shortages, tighten rations, and trim expenses."

sentences.zh: 是故誠遇期運，則雖陶唐、殷湯有所不變；

translations.literal: Therefore if one truly meets such a destined cycle, then even Tao Tang and Yin Tang would have things they could not change;
translations.idiomatic: When destiny truly runs its course, not even rulers like Yao and Tang could alter it;

sentences.zh: 苟非期運，則宋、衛之君，諸侯之相，猶能有感。

translations.literal: if it is not such a cycle, then the lords of Song and Wei, ministers among the feudal lords, can still move Heaven by their conduct."
translations.idiomatic: if it is not fixed fate, even lesser lords and regional ministers can still sway Heaven's response."

sentences.zh: 唯陛下審其所由，以盡其理，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine the causes thereof and exhaust their principles—then the realm will be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty weighs those causes and follows them through, the world will be profoundly blessed."

sentences.zh: 臣生長蓽門，不逮異物，雖有賢才，所未接識，不敢瞽言妄舉，無以疇答聖問。

translations.literal: Your servant was born and raised at a brushwood gate and does not encounter extraordinary things; though there are worthy talents, those I have not met and come to know—I dare not speak blindly or recommend rashly, and have no way to match an answer to the sage question."
translations.idiomatic: I was raised in humble quarters and have met few extraordinary men; though talent exists, I know none of it at first hand, and I dare not babble names at random—I cannot adequately answer Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」擢為太子舍人，除聞喜令。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to crown prince attendant and appointed magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to gentleman attendant to the heir apparent and given the magistracy of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 時天子留心政道，又吳寇新平，天下乂安，上《太康頌》以美晉德。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was attentive to the way of government; moreover the Wu foe had newly been pacified and the realm was peaceful and secure; he presented the "Taikang Eulogy" to praise Jin's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then devoted to sound rule; Wu had just been subdued and the empire was calm. Yu submitted the "Hymn of Great Concord" to celebrate Jin's virtue.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: The text begins:

sentences.zh: :於休上古，人之資始。

translations.literal: Oh splendid—high antiquity, the beginning that sustains mankind."
translations.idiomatic: O glorious primeval age, cradle of human life."

sentences.zh: 四隩咸宅，萬國同軌。

translations.literal: The four corners all had their dwellings; the myriad states shared one track."
translations.idiomatic: Every quarter had its home; myriad kingdoms rolled on one axle."

sentences.zh: 有漢不競，喪亂靡紀。

translations.literal: Han lacked vigor; loss and chaos knew no order."
translations.idiomatic: Han lost its strength; ruin reigned without rule."

sentences.zh: 畿服外叛，侯衛內圮。

translations.literal: The domains beyond the capital rebelled outward; the protective lords collapsed inward."
translations.idiomatic: The heartland's ties frayed beyond the capital; the feudal bulwarks crumbled within."

sentences.zh: 天難既降，時惟鞠凶。

translations.literal: Heaven's hardship having descended, the times knew only extreme misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's scourge had fallen; the age knew deepest woe."

sentences.zh: 龍戰獸爭，分裂遐邦。

translations.literal: Dragons battled and beasts contended; distant lands split apart."
translations.idiomatic: Hosts clashed like dragons and beasts; the realm shattered into rival states."

sentences.zh: 備僭岷蜀，度逆海東。

translations.literal: Bei usurped authority in Min-Shu; Du rebelled east of the sea."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei seized the throne in Shu; Gongsun Du defied the court beyond the eastern sea."

sentences.zh: 權乃緣間，割據三江。

translations.literal: Quan then exploited the interval and carved out control of the three rivers."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan seized the opening and held the lands between the Three Rivers."

sentences.zh: 明明上帝，臨下有赫。

translations.literal: Bright, bright High God—overseeing below with awesome majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Radiant God on high, whose awe-filled gaze rests on the world below."

sentences.zh: 乃宣皇威，致天之辟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he displayed imperial might and carried out Heaven's punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Then royal majesty blazed forth, executing Heaven's judgments."

sentences.zh: 奮武遼隧，罪人斯獲。

translations.literal: He roused arms at Liaosui; the guilty man was thereupon captured."
translations.idiomatic: War flared at Liaosui and the culprits were seized."

sentences.zh: 撫定朝鮮，奄征韓、貊。

translations.literal: He pacified Korea and broadly campaigned against Han and Mo."
translations.idiomatic: Korea was brought to peace; Han and Mo were swept into submission."

sentences.zh: 文既應期，席捲梁、益。

translations.literal: When Wen answered the appointed hour, he rolled up Liang and Yi like a mat."
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen's hour came, Liang and Yi were swept away like a mat."

sentences.zh: 元憝委命，九夷重譯。

translations.literal: The arch rebel surrendered his fate; the nine Yi relayed interpreters."
translations.idiomatic: The chief traitor yielded his doom; barbarians from nine quarters arrived through successive interpreters."

sentences.zh: 邛、冉、哀牢，是焉底績。

translations.literal: Qiong, Ran, and Ailao—there his achievements were completed."
translations.idiomatic: From Qiong and Ran to Ailao—there his triumphs were sealed."

sentences.zh: 我皇之登，二國既平。

translations.literal: At our emperor's accession, the two states were already pacified."
translations.idiomatic: When our sovereign ascended, both rival realms had been crushed."

sentences.zh: 靡適不懷，以育群生。

translations.literal: None whom he faced did he fail to cherish; thereby he nurtured the multitude of lives."
translations.idiomatic: None lay beyond his embrace; he nourished every living being."

sentences.zh: 吳乃負固，放命南冥。

translations.literal: Wu then relied on stubborn terrain and cast aside its mandate in the southern depths."
translations.idiomatic: Wu clung to natural defenses and defied Heaven's charge in the southern deeps."

sentences.zh: 聲教未暨，弗及王靈。

translations.literal: Sound and teaching had not reached them; they did not attain the royal numen."
translations.idiomatic: Our moral sway had not reached them; awe of the throne fell short."

sentences.zh: 皇震其威，赫如雷霆。

translations.literal: The emperor shook his might, brilliant as thunder and lightning."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial majesty cracked like thunder."

sentences.zh: 截彼江、沔，荊、舒以清。

translations.literal: He blocked the Yangzi and Han; Jing and Shu were thereby cleared."
translations.idiomatic: He bridled the great rivers; Jing and Shu were swept clean."

sentences.zh: 邈矣聖皇，參乾兩離。

translations.literal: Far-reaching is the sage emperor—paired with Qian and twinned with Li."
translations.idiomatic: Lofty stands the sage emperor—twinned with Heaven and matched with the sun."

sentences.zh: 陶化以正，取亂以奇。

translations.literal: He molds transformation with rectitude and seizes disorder with surprise."
translations.idiomatic: He shapes the age toward order and masters chaos with audacity."

sentences.zh: 耀武六旬，輿徒不疲。

translations.literal: He displayed arms for sixty days; the hosts on foot did not tire."
translations.idiomatic: For sixty days he showed his might; the armies marched on unwearied."

sentences.zh: 飲至數實，幹旄無虧。

translations.literal: They drank the victory toast and tallies were full; the great pennants knew no lack."
translations.idiomatic: Victory feasts were poured and counts completed; the royal banners flew without blemish."

sentences.zh: 洋洋四海，率禮和樂。

translations.literal: Vast are the four seas; all follow ritual, harmony, and music."
translations.idiomatic: The seas stretch wide; all live by rites in joyful concord."

sentences.zh: 穆穆宮廟，歌雍詠鑠。

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn are the palace temples; they sing "Yong" and chant "Shuo."
translations.idiomatic: Solemn stand the ancestral shrines; hymns of Yong and Shuo resound.

sentences.zh: 光天之下，莫匪帝略。

translations.literal: Beneath the brilliant Heaven, nothing lies beyond the emperor's design."
translations.idiomatic: Under the shining sky, nothing escapes the sovereign's plan."

sentences.zh: 窮發反景，承正受朔。

translations.literal: The farthest north where winter never thaws turns toward the returning light; they receive rectitude and accept the calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Even sunless poles and backward lands accept our calendar and bow to the true throne."

sentences.zh: 龍馬騤騤，風于華陽。

translations.literal: Dragon horses prance in glory; the wind sweeps Huayang."
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-like steeds thunder past; the gale rolls across Huayang."

sentences.zh: 弓矢橐服，干戈戢藏。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows are bagged and cased; shields and spears are gathered away."
translations.idiomatic: Bows and arrows are stowed in quivers; arms are stacked in the arsenal."

sentences.zh: 嚴嚴南金，業業餘皇。

translations.literal: Stately is the southern bronze; towering are the Yuhuang dreadnoughts."
translations.idiomatic: Gleaming southern metal; tall ride the great war-junks."

sentences.zh: 雄劍班朝，造舟為梁。

translations.literal: Heroic swords rank at court; ships are joined to form a bridge."
translations.idiomatic: Keen blades fill the court; hulls are chained to span the stream."

sentences.zh: 聖明有造，實代天工。

translations.literal: Sage clarity brings creation; it truly stands in for Heaven's crafting."
translations.idiomatic: The sage king shapes the age; he truly acts as Heaven's artisan."

sentences.zh: 天地不違，黎元時邕。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth do not oppose him; the black-haired people enjoy timely peace."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth stay true to him; the common folk dwell in harmony."

sentences.zh: 三務斯協，用底厥庸。

translations.literal: The three great tasks accord together; thereby his merit reaches its fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: The three great duties align; his achievement finds its perfect close."

sentences.zh: 既遠其跡，將明其蹤。

translations.literal: Already distant are his footsteps; yet ever brighter shine his traces."
translations.idiomatic: His steps recede into time; his trail glows clearer still."

sentences.zh: 喬山惟嶽，望帝之封。

translations.literal: Mount Qiao stands as a peak—there Wang Di received his mound."
translations.idiomatic: Mount Qiao rises like a sacred summit—there the Wang emperor won his tomb."

sentences.zh: 猗歟聖帝，胡不封哉！

translations.literal: Oh, glorious sage emperor—how could we fail to honor you with a peak!"
translations.idiomatic: O radiant sage sovereign—how could we not crown you with a sacred mount!"

sentences.zh: 以母憂解職。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，召補尚書郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned to fill the post of gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to serve as a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠陳勰掘地得古尺，尚書奏：「今尺長於古尺，宜以古為正。

translations.literal: The master artisan of the Directorate of Palace Construction, Chen Xie, dug in the earth and obtained an ancient foot-rule; the Masters of Writing memorialized: "The present foot is longer than the ancient foot—it is fitting to take the ancient as correct."
translations.idiomatic: Chief builder Chen Xie unearthed an old ruler. The Masters of Writing reported: "Today's measure exceeds the ancient one; we should adopt the ancient standard."

sentences.zh: 」潘嶽以為慣用已久，不宜復改。

translations.literal: " Pan Yue held that customary use had lasted long and it was not fitting to change it again.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue argued that people had used the current measure too long to alter it now.

sentences.zh: 虞駁曰：「昔聖人有以見天下之賾而擬其形容，象物制器，以存時用。

translations.literal: Yu objected, saying: "Of old the sages had means to perceive the hidden depths of all under Heaven and model their forms and images; they imitated things to fashion instruments, thereby preserving timely utility."
translations.idiomatic: Yu rejoined: "The ancient sages read the world's hidden patterns and shaped them in images; they modeled tools after things to serve the needs of the age."

sentences.zh: 故參天兩地，以正算數之紀；

translations.literal: Therefore they matched three with Heaven and two with Earth to rectify the reckoning of numbers;
translations.idiomatic: So they aligned three with heaven and two with earth to fix the system of reckoning;

sentences.zh: 依律計分，以定長短之度。

translations.literal: they relied on the pitch pipes to calculate fractions, thereby fixing the measures of long and short."
translations.idiomatic: they derived fractions from the standard pipes to set the units of length."

sentences.zh: 其作之也有則，故用之也有征。

translations.literal: Their fashioning of these things had norms; therefore their application of them had verification."
translations.idiomatic: Their creation followed fixed rules, so practice could be tested against truth."

sentences.zh: 考步兩儀，則天地無所隱其情；

translations.literal: When one examines and paces the Two Forms, Heaven and Earth nowhere hide their disposition;
translations.idiomatic: Calibrate yin and yang, and Heaven and Earth conceal nothing;

sentences.zh: 准正三辰，則懸象無所容其謬；

translations.literal: when one levels and corrects the Three Luminaries, the suspended celestial bodies nowhere tolerate error."
translations.idiomatic: align sun, moon, and stars, and the heavens admit no mistake."

sentences.zh: 施之金石，則音韻和諧；

translations.literal: Apply them to metal and stone, then tones and rhymes are harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: Apply them to bells and stones, and music rings true;

sentences.zh: 措之規矩，則器用合宜。

translations.literal: set them in compass and square, then vessels and tools are fitting."
translations.idiomatic: fit them to rule and square, and every implement suits its task."

sentences.zh: 一本不差而萬物皆正，及其差也，事皆反是。

translations.literal: When one root is not wrong, myriad things are all correct; when it errs, affairs all reverse this."
translations.idiomatic: Hold one true standard and everything aligns; let it slip and all goes awry."

sentences.zh: 今尺長於古尺幾於半寸，樂府用之，律呂不合；

translations.literal: Now the foot is longer than the ancient foot by nearly half an inch; the Music Bureau uses it—the pitch pipes do not match;
translations.idiomatic: Today's foot exceeds the old by nearly half an inch. The Music Bureau follows it, so the scales fall out of tune;

sentences.zh: 史官用之，曆象失占；

translations.literal: the historians use it—calendrical phenomena lose prognostication;
translations.idiomatic: the clerks of history rely on it, and celestial reckoning fails;

sentences.zh: 醫署用之，孔穴乖錯。

translations.literal: the medical office uses it—the acupuncture points are wrong and misplaced."
translations.idiomatic: physicians use it, and needle points go astray."

sentences.zh: 此三者，度量之所由生，得失之所取征，皆絓閡而不得通，故宜改今而從古也。

translations.literal: These three are where measures arise and where gain and loss take verification—all are blocked and cannot flow through; therefore it is fitting to change the present and follow the ancient."
translations.idiomatic: These three anchor measurement and test right from wrong; all are jammed and fail. We should abandon the present ruler and restore the ancient length."

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之制，同律度量衡，仲尼之訓，謹權審度。

translations.literal: The institutions of Tang and Yu unified pitch pipes, measures, volumes, and balances; the teachings of Zhongni say to weigh carefully and examine measures."
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Yao and Shun unified pitch, length, volume, and weight; Confucius taught scrupulous balances and careful measures."

sentences.zh: 今兩尺並用，不可謂之同；

translations.literal: Now two feet are used together—this cannot be called 'same';
translations.idiomatic: Two rulers at once cannot be called unity;

sentences.zh: 知失而行，不可謂之謹。

translations.literal: knowing error yet proceeding—this cannot be called 'careful.'
translations.idiomatic: Persisting while knowing it is wrong cannot be called diligence."

sentences.zh: 不同不謹，是謂謬法，非所以軌物垂則，示人之極。

translations.literal: Neither 'same' nor 'careful'—this is called mistaken law; it is not the means to regulate things, hang down norms, and show people the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Neither unified nor careful—that is a broken statute, unfit to guide the world or set the standard for men."

sentences.zh: 凡物有多而易改，亦有少而難變，亦有改而致煩，有變而之簡。

translations.literal: Among things, some are many and easy to change; some are few and hard to change; some changes bring vexation; some changes lead to simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: Some things abound yet change easily; others are few yet stubborn; some reforms breed trouble; others simplify."

sentences.zh: 度量是人所常用，而長短非人所戀惜，是多而易改者也。

translations.literal: Measures are what people constantly use, while long and short are not what people cling to—this is the case of many and easy to change."
translations.idiomatic: We handle measures daily, yet no one hoards a favorite inch—that makes them plentiful and easy to correct."

sentences.zh: 正失於得，反邪于正，一時之變，永世無二，是變而之簡者也。

translations.literal: Correcting error into gain, returning wrong to rectitude—a single moment's change, forever without a second—this is change that leads to simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: Right a wrong in one stroke and the standard lasts for all time—the simplest reform of all."

sentences.zh: 憲章成式，不失舊物，季末苟合之制，異端雜亂之用，當以時厘改，貞夫一者也。

translations.literal: Statutes and models into completed patterns do not lose old things; makeshift systems of a declining age and mongrel, chaotic practices ought to be rectified in their time—this is holding fast to the one."
translations.idiomatic: Anchor your norms in stable forms without betraying ancient usage; patchwork rules and hodgepodge tools deserve timely cleanup—hold to the single true measure."

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜如所奏。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks it fitting to act as memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should adopt the memorial as written."

sentences.zh: 」又表論封禪，見《禮志》。

translations.literal: " He also submitted a memorial discussing the feng and shan sacrifices—see the "Treatise on Rites."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on the Feng and Shan sacrifices; see the Treatise on Rites."

sentences.zh: 虞以漢末喪亂，譜傳多亡失，雖其子孫不能言其先祖，撰《族姓昭穆》十卷，上疏進之，以為足以備物致用，廣多聞之益。

translations.literal: Because at the end of Han there was turmoil and chaos, genealogical records were mostly lost—even their descendants could not speak of their remote ancestors; he compiled "Clan Surnames: Altars and Order" in ten fascicles and submitted it by memorial, thinking it sufficient to prepare implements and put them to use, extending the benefit of wide learning."
translations.idiomatic: After Han's collapse destroyed most pedigrees—even sons could not name their forebears—Yu compiled the ten-scroll Clan Lineages: Altars and Order and presented it, holding that it would equip practical use and broaden scholarly knowledge."

sentences.zh: 以定品違法，為司徒所劾，詔原之。

translations.literal: Because in fixing rank assessments he violated the law, he was impeached by the Minister of Education; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education impeached him for irregularities in evaluating ranks, but an imperial pardon spared him.

sentences.zh: 時太廟初建，詔普增位一等。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Ancestral Temple was first erected; an edict universally raised everyone one rank in grade.
translations.idiomatic: When the great ancestral shrine was first dedicated, an edict raised every official one step in rank.

sentences.zh: 後以主者承詔失旨，改除之。

translations.literal: Later, because the responsible official in implementing the edict missed its intent, it was altered and rescinded.
translations.idiomatic: The benefit was later withdrawn when officers mishandled the edict's meaning.

sentences.zh: 虞上表曰：「臣聞昔之聖明，不愛千乘之國而惜桐葉之信，所以重至尊之命而達于萬國之誠也。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the sage rulers of old did not spare a state of a thousand chariots yet cherished the trust shown by a paulownia leaf—thereby honoring the commands of the supreme one and extending sincerity to the myriad states."
translations.idiomatic: Yu wrote: "Ancient sages prized a child's promise sealed with a leaf above a thousand-chariot realm—honoring the sovereign word and binding all lands in good faith."

sentences.zh: 前《乙巳赦書》，遠稱先帝遺惠餘澤，普增位一等，以酬四海欣戴之心。

translations.literal: The recent 'Yisi Amnesty Edict' praised from afar the late emperor's lingering grace and surplus bounty and universally raised rank one grade, to repay the joyful support of the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: The recent Yisi amnesty cited our late sovereign's lingering kindness and raised every rank one step to reward the realm's loyal joy."

sentences.zh: 驛書班下，被於遠近，莫不鳥騰魚躍，喜蒙德澤。

translations.literal: Relay edicts were promulgated far and near; none failed to soar like birds and leap like fish, rejoicing to receive virtue's moisture."
translations.idiomatic: Courier proclamations reached every quarter; people rejoiced like birds aloft and fish in spray, grateful for the imperial rain."

sentences.zh: 今一旦更以主者思文不審，收既往之詔，奪已澍之施，臣之愚心竊以為不可。

translations.literal: Now suddenly those in charge have reconsidered the wording carelessly, rescinding the edict already issued and revoking what has already been granted; your servant's foolish heart privately holds this to be impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Now that those responsible have second-guessed the wording and withdrawn the promulgated edict and canceled benefits already distributed, I respectfully believe this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict approving it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal in an edict.

sentences.zh: 元康中，遷吳王友。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era he was transferred to the post of Companion to the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuankang period he was promoted to Companion to the Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 時荀顗撰《新禮》，使虞討論得失而後施行。

translations.literal: At that time Xun Yi was compiling the New Rites; he had Yu discuss what should be kept or discarded before putting it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xun Yi was drafting the New Rites and assigned Yu to debate its strengths and weaknesses before implementation.

sentences.zh: 元皇后崩，杜預奏：「諒暗之制，乃自上古，是以高宗無服喪之文，而唯文稱不言。

translations.literal: When Empress Yuan died, Du Yu memorialized: "The regulations for 'liang'an' [mourning seclusion] reach back to high antiquity; therefore Gaozong has no passage about wearing mourning garments, and the Documents only says he 'did not speak.'
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yuan passed away, Du Yu submitted a memorial: "The rule of secluded mourning goes back to remote antiquity, which is why the Documents record no formal mourning dress for Gaozong—only that he remained silent."

sentences.zh: 漢文限三十六日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han fixed it at thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi capped it at thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 魏氏以降，既虞為節。

translations.literal: From the Wei dynasty onward, they took the Yu[-period observance] as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei onward, the mourning span was keyed to the Yu observance.

sentences.zh: 皇太子與國為體，理宜釋服，卒哭便除。

translations.literal: The crown prince is of one body with the state; by principle he ought to lay aside mourning dress and remove it when the weeping sacrifice ends.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heir shares one fate with the realm, he should end mourning and shed mourning garments at the conclusion of the crying rites.

sentences.zh: 」虞答預書曰：「唐稱遏密，殷雲諒暗，各舉事以為名，非既葬有殊降。

translations.literal: Yu replied to Du Yu in a letter: "Tang spoke of 'e-mi' [silencing music]; Yin spoke of 'liang'an'; each named a concrete practice, not a special reduction after burial.
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered Du Yu's letter: "The Tang tradition speaks of silencing music; the Yin tradition speaks of secluded mourning—each names a particular observance, not a lesser grade tied to post-burial timing."

sentences.zh: 周室以來，謂之喪服。

translations.literal: Since the house of Zhou it has been called mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou onward this has been termed mourning apparel.

sentences.zh: 喪服者，以服表喪。

translations.literal: 'Mourning dress' means using garments to display mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning garments exist to outwardly signify bereavement.

sentences.zh: 今帝者一日萬機，太子監撫之重，以宜奪禮，葬訖除服，變制通理，垂典將來，何必附之于古，使老儒致爭哉！

translations.literal: Today the sovereign faces myriad affairs in a single day, and the crown prince bears the weight of oversight and nurturing; it is fitting to curtail ritual propriety, remove garments once burial is finished, alter the system to accord with principle, and leave a norm for posterity—why insist on grafting everything onto antiquity and setting old scholars at odds!"
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor overwhelmed daily and the heir bearing the burden of guardianship, shortening the rites, ending dress after the funeral, and adjusting the code to match reason would establish a precedent for the future—there is no need to bind every detail to the past and invite quarrels among aged classicists!"

sentences.zh: 」皇太孫尚薨，有司奏「御服齊衰期」。

translations.literal: When the imperial great-grandson Shang died, the authorities memorialized that 'the sovereign should wear zicui-grade mourning for one year.'
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial great-grandson Shang died, officials requested that the emperor observe one year of zicui mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔令博士議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the academicians to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commanded the court scholars to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 虞曰：「太子生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Yu said: "If, when the crown prince was born, he was invested with the rites due an adult, then the logic of 'shang' [child mourning] is already removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued: "If the crown prince was welcomed into the world with adult rites, the category of child-death mourning no longer applies."

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服全，非以年也。

translations.literal: The great-grandson likewise embodies the ruler and bears the heavy succession; completeness of mourning comes from the dignity of his station, not from his years."
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson likewise embodies the sovereign and shoulders the succession—his full mourning obligation rests on his rank, not on his age."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court accepted his view.
translations.idiomatic: His recommendation was adopted.

sentences.zh: 虞又議玉輅、兩社事，見《輿服志》。

translations.literal: Yu also debated the royal jade carriage and the twin soil altars; see the Treatise on Carriages and Dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yu further argued the cases of the imperial jade chariot and the paired soil altars—details appear in the Treatise on Carriages and Vestments.

sentences.zh: 後曆秘書監、衛尉卿，從惠帝幸長安。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of the Guards, and accompanied Emperor Hui to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He subsequently rose through Secretary Director and Minister of the Guards, following Emperor Hui on the journey to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及東軍來迎，百官奔散，遂流離鄠、杜之間，轉入南山中，糧絕饑甚，拾橡實而食之。

translations.literal: When the eastern army came to escort [the court], the officials fled and scattered; he wandered destitute between Hu and Du, then turned into the southern hills; when provisions ran out he starved severely and gathered acorns to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When troops from the east arrived to receive the emperor, the bureaucracy scattered; Yu drifted between Hu and Du and withdrew into the Zhongnan hills, and when food gave out he nearly starved, subsisting on fallen acorns.

sentences.zh: 後得還洛，曆光祿勳、太常卿。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return to Luoyang and served in succession as Minister of the Household for All Purposes and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually made it back to Luoyang and held successive posts as Superintendent of the Household and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時懷帝親郊。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Huai personally performed the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure Emperor Huai conducted the suburban offering in person.

sentences.zh: 自元康以來，不親郊祀，禮儀弛廢。

translations.literal: Since the Yuankang era, emperors had not personally attended suburban sacrifices, and ritual observance had slackened and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuankang onward no ruler had personally celebrated the suburban rites, and ceremonial discipline had fallen apart.

sentences.zh: 虞考正舊典，法物粲然。

translations.literal: Yu collated and corrected the old statutes, and the ritual paraphernalia shone in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Yu restored the classical precedents, and the regalia again appeared complete and correct.

sentences.zh: 及洛京荒亂，盜竊縱橫，人饑相食。

translations.literal: When the Luoyang capital fell into chaos and turmoil, theft ran rampant and starving people devoured one another.
translations.idiomatic: As the eastern capital descended into chaos, banditry spread unchecked and famine drove men to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 虞素清貧，遂以餒卒。

translations.literal: Yu had always been poor and destitute, and so died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, chronically impoverished, eventually starved to death.

sentences.zh: 虞撰《文章志》四卷，注解《三輔決錄》，又撰古文章，類聚區分為三十卷，名曰《流別集》，各為之論，辭理愜當，為世所重。

translations.literal: Yu compiled the Literary Records in four volumes, annotated the Records of the Three Metropolitan Regions Resolved, and also assembled ancient writings, sorting them into thirty fascicles under the title Collected Writings by Genre, appending a critical essay to each section; the diction and reasoning were apt and fitting, and the work was highly esteemed in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the four-juan Literary Gazetteer, annotated the Records of the Three Metropolitan Regions Resolved, and compiled thirty fascicles of classical prose arranged by genre as the Collected Writings by Genre, each section with its own essay—the prose and argument were judged sound, and the collection carried great prestige.

sentences.zh: 虞善觀玄象，嘗謂友人曰：「今天下方亂，避難之國，其唯涼土乎！

translations.literal: Yu was skilled at reading celestial signs; he once told a friend: "The realm is falling into chaos; of lands where one might flee for refuge, surely only the Liang region will do!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu excelled at interpreting the heavens; he once remarked to a companion, "All under heaven is sliding toward turmoil—the only haven worth fleeing to may be the northwestern frontier."

sentences.zh: 」性愛士人，有表薦者，恆為其辭。

translations.literal: He naturally cherished literati; whenever someone submitted a memorial of recommendation, he habitually drafted the wording.
translations.idiomatic: He loved nurturing scholars and routinely composed the language whenever anyone forwarded a recommendation memorial.

sentences.zh: 東平太叔廣樞機清辯，廣談，虞不能對；

translations.literal: Taishu Guang of Dongping was sharp and eloquent in debate; in wide-ranging conversation Yu could not answer him.
translations.idiomatic: Taishu Guang of Dongping was swift and brilliant in repartee; in expansive talk Yu could not hold his own.

sentences.zh: 虞筆，廣不能答；

translations.literal: When Yu took up the brush, Guang could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Yu wrote, Guang had no comeback.

sentences.zh: 更相嗤笑，紛然於世雲。

translations.literal: They ridiculed each other in turn, and the story buzzed through society.
translations.idiomatic: They traded barbs, and gossip about it flew everywhere.

sentences.zh: 束晳

translations.literal: Shu Xi
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi

sentences.zh: 束晳，字廣微，陽平元城人，漢太子太傅疏廣之後也。

translations.literal: Shu Xi, courtesy name Guangwei, was a native of Yuancheng in Yangping and a descendant of Shu Guang, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent under the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi (courtesy name Guangwei) came from Yuancheng in Yangping and traced his line to Shu Guang, Grand Tutor to the Han heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 王莽末，廣曾孫孟達避難，自東海徙居沙鹿山南，因去疏之足，遂改姓焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Wang Mang's reign, Guang's great-grandson Mengda fled disaster, moving from Donghai to dwell south of Mount Shalu; by dropping the 'foot' component from the character Shu he changed the surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, Guang's great-grandson Mengda escaped the turmoil, relocating from Donghai to the south of Mount Shalu; he dropped the lower portion of the Shu clan glyph and took the homophonous surname Shu that means "bundle," distinguishing his branch from the original Shu.

sentences.zh: 祖混，隴西太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hun served as Administrator of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hun was governor of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父龕，馮翊太守，並有名譽。

translations.literal: His father Kan served as Administrator of Pingyi; both men enjoyed reputations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan governed Pingyi; both were widely respected.

sentences.zh: 晳博學多聞，與兄璆俱知名。

translations.literal: Xi was widely learned and well informed; he and his elder brother Qiu were both celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: Xi possessed immense erudition and shared renown with his older brother Qiu.

sentences.zh: 少游國學，或問博士曹志曰：「當今好學者誰乎？

translations.literal: In his youth he studied at the national academy; someone asked Academician Cao Zhi: "Who nowadays loves learning?"
translations.idiomatic: While studying at the imperial academy as a young man, he heard an acquaintance ask Academician Cao Zhi who among contemporaries truly loved scholarship.

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「陽平束廣微好學不倦，人莫及也。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi said: "Shu Guangwei of Yangping loves learning tirelessly; no one can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi answered, "Shu Guangwei of Yangping never tires of study—no one equals him."

sentences.zh: 」還鄉里，察孝廉，舉茂才，皆不就。

translations.literal: Xi returned to his home district; he was nominated Filial and Incorrupt and recommended as Abundant Talent, but accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he received nominations as Filial and Incorrupt and as Abundant Talent and declined both.

sentences.zh: 璆娶石鑒從女，棄之，鑒以為憾，諷州郡公府不得辟，故晳等久不得調。

translations.literal: Qiu married a cousin's daughter of Shi Jian but divorced her; Jian nursed a grudge and hinted that prefectures and central offices should not summon them, so Xi and the others long went without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu wed a niece of Shi Jian and later cast her aside; the insulted Jian quietly pressured local and capital authorities not to recruit the brothers, leaving Xi long unemployed.

sentences.zh: 太康中，郡界大旱，晳為邑人請雨，三日而雨注，眾謂晳誠感，為作歌曰：「束先生，通神明，請天三日甘雨零。

translations.literal: During the Taikang era a severe drought struck the commandery; Xi prayed for rain on behalf of the townsfolk, and after three days a deluge fell; the crowd said Xi's sincerity had moved Heaven and composed a song: "Master Shu reaches gods and spirits; praying to Heaven three days, sweet rain sprinkles down.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taikang period the district suffered a terrible drought; Xi led prayers for the community, and rain poured three days later—people credited his sincerity and sang, "Master Shu moves heaven and earth; three days of prayer brought gentle rain."

sentences.zh: 我黍以育，我稷以生。

translations.literal: Our millet thereby grows; our grain thereby lives.
translations.idiomatic: Our crops revive and our grain sprouts anew.

sentences.zh: 何以疇之？

translations.literal: How shall we repay it?
translations.idiomatic: How can we repay such grace?

sentences.zh: 報束長生。

translations.literal: Repay Master Shu, who lives long."
translations.idiomatic: We repay Master Shu, who grants us long life."

sentences.zh: 」晳與衛恆厚善，聞恆遇禍，自本郡赴喪。

translations.literal: Xi was on cordial terms with Wei Heng; when he learned Heng had met disaster, he hurried from his home commandery to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Wei Heng were close friends; hearing of Heng's violent death, Xi raced from his native commandery to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《勸農》及《餅》諸賦，文頗鄙俗，時人薄之。

translations.literal: He once composed the "Encourage Agriculture" and "Cakes" rhapsodies among others; the writing was rather vulgar, and people of the time disparaged it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote occasional pieces such as "Encourage Agriculture" and "Cakes"; the style struck contemporaries as coarse, and they dismissed his verse.

sentences.zh: 而性沈退，不慕榮利，作《玄居釋》以擬《客難》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Yet his temperament was retiring and he did not crave glory or profit; he composed "Explanation of Dwelling in Mystery," modeled on "The Guest's Challenge," which begins:
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was withdrawn and unconcerned with fame; he penned "Explanation of Dwelling in Mystery," patterned after "The Guest's Difficulty," opening thus:

sentences.zh: 束晳閒居，門人並侍。

translations.literal: Shu Xi dwelled at leisure while disciples attended him together.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi lived quietly at home, surrounded by students.

sentences.zh: 方下帷深譚，隱-{几}-而咍，含毫散藻，考撰同異，在側者進而問之曰：「蓋聞道尚變通，達者無窮。

translations.literal: They had lowered the curtain for deep discourse; he leaned on the knee-table and laughed softly, brush between his lips as ornate phrases spilled forth, comparing similarities and differences—those beside him stepped forward and asked: "We have heard that the Way esteems adaptability and that the enlightened have no limit.
translations.idiomatic: With the study curtains drawn they plumbed profound topics; he rested against the knee-table, chuckling as he poised his brush and spun polished lines, weighing agreements and disagreements—those nearby pressed him: "We are told the Dao prizes flexibility and that the wise face no dead end."

sentences.zh: 世亂則救其紛，時泰則扶其隆。

translations.literal: When the age is chaotic one remedies its confusion; when the times are prosperous one upholds their grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: In chaotic ages one untangles disorder; in flourishing eras one sustains their heights."

sentences.zh: 振天維以贊百務，熙帝載而鼓皇風。

translations.literal: Raise the celestial net to assist the myriad tasks; brighten the emperor's burden and stir the august wind.
translations.idiomatic: Spread heaven's guiding net to aid every undertaking; illuminate the sovereign's enterprise and quicken the imperial ethos."

sentences.zh: 生則率土樂其存，死則宇內哀其終。

translations.literal: Living, the whole realm rejoices in his survival; dying, all within the seas mourns his end.
translations.idiomatic: While he lives, the land delights in his presence; when he dies, the world laments his passing."

sentences.zh: 是以君子屈己伸道，不恥幹時。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman bends himself to extend the Way and is not ashamed to serve the times.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the noble person restrains self-interest to advance the Way and does not scorn engaging the age."

sentences.zh: 上國有不索何獲之言，《周易》著躍以求進之辭。

translations.literal: The superior state has the saying 'without seeking, what is gained'; the Zhou Changes records leaping upward to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains teach that nothing comes without pursuit; the Classic of Changes praises bold ascent toward appointment."

sentences.zh: 莘老負金鉉以陳烹割之說，齊客當康衢而詠《白水》之詩。

translations.literal: The old man of Shen shouldered the golden cauldron to expound the art of ruling; a Qi visitor stood at the great crossroads chanting "White Water."
translations.idiomatic: The elder of Shen bore the ritual cauldron to lecture on statecraft; a traveler from Qi sang "White Water" in the broad avenue."

sentences.zh: 今先生耽道修藝，嶷然山峙，潛朗通微，洽覽深識，夜兼忘寐之勤，晝騁鑽玄之思，曠年累稔，不墮其志。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, dwell on the Way and refine your arts, standing sheer as a mountain, penetrating brilliance to reach the subtle, harmonizing broad learning with deep insight—by night doubling wakeful diligence, by day racing through thoughts that bore into the mysterious; years and harvests pile up, yet you do not abandon your aim.
translations.idiomatic: Today you immerse yourself in the Dao and polish your skills—aloof as a peak, lucid to the finest grain, pairing vast reading with keen judgment—burning midnight oil and pondering mysteries by daylight; decade after decade you never slacken your purpose."

sentences.zh: 鱗翼成而愈伏，術業優而不試。

translations.literal: Scales and wings fully formed yet you hide deeper; your arts excel yet go untried.
translations.idiomatic: Your talents are fully fledged yet you stay concealed; your craft surpasses others yet never faces trial."

sentences.zh: 乃欲闔櫝辭價，泥蟠深處，永戢琳琅之耀，匿首窮魚之渚，當唐年而慕長沮，邦有道而反甯武。

translations.literal: You would lock the jeweled casket and refuse its price, coil like a dragon in the deepest mud, forever sheathing the gleam of rare gems, hiding your head on the shoal of stranded fish; facing an age like Tang's yet longing for Chang Ju, and though the state possesses the Way you imitate Ning Wu's folly.
translations.idiomatic: You mean to seal away treasure in its box, burrow into silt, forever dimming jade radiance and skulking like a fish beached on a shoal—you admire Chang Ju even under enlightened rule and mimic Ning Wu's folly though the kingdom knows good government."

sentences.zh: 識彼迷此，愚竊不取。

translations.literal: Seeing their path yet lost in yours—this foolish heart cannot approve.
translations.idiomatic: They understand one course yet cling to another—I cannot endorse such confusion."

sentences.zh: 若乃士以援登，進必待求，附勢之黨橫擢，則林藪之彥不抽，丹墀步紈誇之童，東野遺白顛之叟。

translations.literal: If gentlemen ascend only when pulled aloft and advancement waits on solicitation—when factions of the mighty promote favorites at will, worthies of grove and marsh are never drawn forth; on the cinnabar steps swagger youths boasting silken finery, while white-haired elders languish in the eastern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: If office rides on patronage and promotion requires canvassing—when power brokers yank up allies, recluses never surface; scarlet stairs teem with silk-clad striplings while hoary sages rot in rustic lanes."

sentences.zh: 盍亦因數都而事博陸，憑鷁首以涉洪流，蹈翠雲以駭逸龍，振光耀以驚沈鰌。

translations.literal: Why not ride several capitals' momentum to serve Bolu, trust a bird-prow vessel to cross the flood, tread emerald clouds to startle soaring dragons, flash radiance to alarm river monsters lurking below?
translations.idiomatic: Why not harness metropolitan influence like Huo Guang, sail the torrent with a swift prow, stride rainbow vapor to rouse sleeping dragons, or blaze like lightning to wake lazy leviathans?"

sentences.zh: 徒屈蟠于陷井，眄天路而不遊，學既積而身困，夫何為乎秘丘。

translations.literal: To coil vainly in a pitfall, gaze toward heaven's road yet never wander—learning piles up while the body remains trapped—what use is hiding on a secret hill!
translations.idiomatic: To curl in a snare while staring at the sky—learning amassed yet life imprisoned—what profit lies in that lonely mound!"

sentences.zh: 且歲不我與，時若奔駟，有來無反，難得易失。

translations.literal: Moreover the years do not wait for us; time gallops like swift teams; it arrives and does not return—hard to seize, easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the seasons spare no one; hours gallop like paired horses—once gone they never return, easily squandered and scarcely regained."

sentences.zh: 先生不知盱豫之讖悔遲，而忘夫朋盍之義務疾，亦豈能登海湄而抑東流之水，臨虞泉而招西歸之日？

translations.literal: Sir, you ignore the omen of playful hesitation that warns of late regret, and forget how Peng's companionship demands swift action—how could you climb the ocean strand and dam the east-flowing stream, or stand by the Yu Springs and summon the sun returning west?
translations.idiomatic: You disregard the warning against procrastination and forget that fellowship obliges speed—do you think you can climb the beach and block the eastern tide, or halt at the sundial pool and beckon the setting sun?"

sentences.zh: 徒以曲畏為梏，儒學自桎，囚大道於環堵，苦形骸於蓬室。

translations.literal: You merely treat twisted fear as fetters, bind yourself with Confucian doctrine, imprison the Great Way within a ring of walls, and torment your body in a weed-roofed hut.
translations.idiomatic: You let crooked fear become shackles, let classical study cage you, trap the great Dao inside a mud wall, and torture your flesh in a thatched cell."

sentences.zh: 豈若托身權戚，憑勢假力，擇棲芳林，飛不待翼，夕宿七娥之房，朝享五鼎之食，匡三正則太階平，贊五教而玉繩直。
