translations.literal: How can that compare to entrusting yourself to powerful kin, borrowing rank and borrowed strength, choosing a perch in fragrant woods, flying without awaiting wings, lodging at night in chambers fit for the Seven Lofty Ladies, dining at dawn from five sacrificial tripods, aiding the Three Alignments so the Grand Stairway lies level, assisting the Five Teachings so the Jade Cord hangs straight?
translations.idiomatic: Why not ally with great houses, ride influence and borrowed force, nest among flowering groves, soar without grown wings, spend nights in palace bowers and mornings at bronze cauldrons—steady the three cosmic norms so the Grand Stair is calm and uphold the five moral bonds so the celestial cord stays true?"

sentences.zh: 孰若茹藿餐蔬，終身自匿哉！」

translations.literal: Who would rather chew bitter herbs and greens, hiding to the end of his days!"
translations.idiomatic: Who prefers husks and wild greens while burying himself forever!"

sentences.zh: 束子曰：「居！

translations.literal: Master Shu said: "Stay!
translations.idiomatic: Master Shu answered: "Sit quietly!"

sentences.zh: 吾將導爾以君子之道，諭爾以出處之事。

translations.literal: I shall lead you in the way of the gentleman and instruct you in the choice between withdrawal and service.
translations.idiomatic: I will chart for you the path of the noble person and explain how to leave office or take it."

sentences.zh: 爾其明受餘訊，謹聽餘志。

translations.literal: Listen clearly to my teaching and heed my intent with care.
translations.idiomatic: Mark every word of my lesson and attend faithfully to my purpose."

sentences.zh: 昔元一既啟，兩儀肇立，離光夜隱，望舒晝戢，羽族翔林，蟩蛁赴濕，物從性之所安，士樂志之所執，或背豐榮以岩棲，或排蘭闥而求入，在野者龍逸，在朝者鳳集。

translations.literal: Long ago, when the Primal One opened and the Two Modes first stood, the solar radiance hid at night and the moon chariot folded its beams by day; winged kind wheel through forests while crawling things hurry toward moisture—creatures follow where their natures rest easy, and scholars delight in the aims they embrace—some renounce splendor to dwell on crags, others push past orchid gates to seek entry; those in the wild roam like hidden dragons, those at court gather like phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, when chaos parted into yin and yang, sunlight withdrew at nightfall and moonlight dimmed at dawn—birds wheel through the woods and worms seek damp soil; each being settles where instinct leads, just as each scholar cherishes his chosen end—some spurn luxury for cliff hermitage, others shoulder past vermilion doors; recluses coil like unseen dragons, courtiers flock like phoenixes."

sentences.zh: 雖其軌跡不同，而道無貴賤，必安其業，交不相羨，稷、契奮庸以宣道，巢、由洗耳以避禪，同垂不朽之稱，俱入賢者之流。

translations.literal: Though their tracks differ, the Way knows no high or low—each must rest content with his vocation and not envy another; Ji and Qi exerted their offices to proclaim the Way, Chao and Xu washed their ears to decline abdication—alike they earned imperishable renown and both entered the company of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Their roads diverge, yet the Dao shows no rank—each must be satisfied with his lot and refrain from mutual envy. Ji and Qi toiled in office to spread civilization; Chao and Xu cleansed their ears to refuse the throne—both left immortal fame among the sages."

sentences.zh: 參名比譽，誰劣誰優？

translations.literal: Set name beside renown—who is inferior, who superior?
translations.idiomatic: Compare reputations side by side—who then is lesser, who greater?"

sentences.zh: 何必貪與二八為群，而恥為七人之疇乎！

translations.literal: Why crave fellowship with the Twenty-Eight Lodges yet blush at ranking among the Seven Sages!
translations.idiomatic: Why hunger for a place among the starry ministers yet scorn standing with the Seven Worthies!"

sentences.zh: 且道睽而通，士不同趣，吾竊綴處者之末行，未敢聞子之高喻，將忽蒲輪而不眄，夫何權戚之雲附哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the Way may seem estranged yet still connects; scholars pursue different inclinations. I humbly follow the lowly practice of recluses; I dare not embrace your lofty analogy—I would ignore even the rush-wheeled summoning cart—why speak of clinging to powerful kin like clouds!
translations.idiomatic: Even when paths diverge they may converge, and scholars follow diverse callings. I cling to the humble example of hermits; I cannot accept your elevated metaphor—I would pass by the imperial carriage without a glance—so why invoke riding coat-tails of the mighty?"

sentences.zh: 昔周、漢中衰，時難自托，福兆既開，患端亦作，朝游巍峨之宮，夕墜崢嶸之壑，晝笑夜歎，晨華暮落，忠不足以衛己，禍不可以預度，是士諱登朝而競赴林薄。

translations.literal: In days when Zhou and Han declined midcourse, the age offered little footing; omens of fortune opened while calamity's shoots sprouted—morning saw one roaming lofty palaces, evening cast one into jagged chasms; laughing by day, sighing by night; blossom at dawn, fall at dusk—loyalty could not shield the body, disaster defied foresight—so scholars shunned court ascent and raced instead into thickets.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou and Han faltered, fortune and peril intertwined—palaces at dawn, abysses at dusk, laughter turning overnight to lament; loyalty failed to save men and ruin struck without warning—learners avoided the hall of audience and bolted for the brush."

sentences.zh: 或毀名自汙，或不食其祿，比從政於匣笥之龜，譬官者於郊廟之犢，公孫泣涕而辭相，楊雄抗論於赤族。

translations.literal: Some ruined their good names to blacken themselves, some refused stipends—likening officeholding to the tortoise kept in a box, comparing officials to calves tethered for suburban sacrifice; Gongsun wept as he declined the chancellorship; Yang Xiong argued boldly though it meant death for his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Some fouled their reputations on purpose, some spurned salaries—equating power with caged divination turtles or sacrificial calves; Gongsun Hong tearfully refused the seal; Yang Xiong debated execution for his entire kin."

sentences.zh: 今大晉熙隆，六合寧靜。

translations.literal: Now Great Jin flourishes in glory; the six directions lie tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Today Great Jin glows with prosperity and the realm rests undisturbed."

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆止毒，熊羆輟猛，五刑勿用，八紘備整，主無驕肆之怒，臣無犛纓之請，上下相安，率禮從道。

translations.literal: Wasps and scorpions curb their venom; bears and brown bears pause their ferocity; the five punishments need not be applied; the eight bounds stand fully ordered; the ruler shows no wanton wrath; ministers present no vain requests for honors—high and low dwell in peace, all guided by ritual and the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Stingers lose their poison; bears halt their rage; penalties lie unused and the eight directions align; the sovereign indulges no arbitrary fury and ministers beg no empty distinctions—throne and subject coexist peacefully, each treading ritual and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 朝養觸邪之獸，庭有指佞之草，禍戮可以忠逃，寵祿可以順保。

translations.literal: The court nurtures the beast that gores evil; the courtyard grows grass that exposes flattery—execution may be escaped through loyalty; favor and salary may be preserved through compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The palace feeds horned beasts that attack wickedness; the garden sprouts plants that expose sycophants—loyalty shields one from punishment; obedience secures grace."

sentences.zh: 且夫進無險懼，而惟寂之務者，率其性也。

translations.literal: Moreover advancing involves no perilous fear; to devote oneself solely to stillness follows one's nature.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, promotion carries no mortal dread; choosing quietism follows innate disposition."

sentences.zh: 兩可俱是，而舍彼趣此者，從其志也。

translations.literal: When both courses can be right, yet one abandons that and races to this, it follows one's will.
translations.idiomatic: When either path may be justified, yet someone forsakes one for the other, individual intent decides."

sentences.zh: 蓋無為可以解天下之紛，澹泊可以救國家之急，當位者事有所窮，陳策者言有不入，翟璜不能回西鄰之寇，平、勃不能正如意之立，幹木臥而秦師退，四皓起而戚姬泣。

translations.literal: For non-action can unravel the world's snarls; emptiness can relieve a nation's crisis—those in office meet limits to what they can accomplish; those offering counsel find words unwelcome; Zhai Huang could not repel the western neighbor's raid; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not legitimize Ruyi's installation; Duan Ganmu reclined and Qin's army withdrew; the Four Hoary Heads emerged and Lady Qi wept.
translations.idiomatic: Stillness untangles worldly knots; detachment eases dynastic peril—those enthroned reach the end of their means; memorials sometimes fail to persuade; Zhai Huang could not stop western invasions; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not secure Prince Ruyi; Duan Ganmu's mere posture routed Qin troops; the Four Elders rose and Consort Qi wept."

sentences.zh: 夫如是何舍何執，何去何就？

translations.literal: Given this, what should one discard or cling to; where depart, where go?
translations.idiomatic: Under such conditions what is worth grasping or releasing, fleeing or embracing?"

sentences.zh: 謂山岑之林為芳，穀底之莽為臭。

translations.literal: You pronounce forests on mountain crests fragrant and weeds in valley bottoms foul.
translations.idiomatic: You label upland groves sweet and lowland thickets stench."

sentences.zh: 守分任性，唯天所授，鳥不假甲於龜，魚不借足於獸，何必笑孤竹之貧而羨齊景之富！

translations.literal: Keeping to one's lot and following nature—Heaven alone assigns endowment; birds do not borrow armor from turtles, fish do not borrow feet from beasts—why mock Guzhu's poverty yet envy Duke Jing of Qi's wealth!
translations.idiomatic: Hold your station and obey innate bent—Heaven grants each nature; birds never steal tortoise shells for feathers nor fish hooves from beasts—so why ridicule poor Guzhu yet crave Qi Jing's riches!"

sentences.zh: 恥布衣以肆志，甯文裘而拖繡。

translations.literal: They scorn plain cloth while indulging ambition; they would rather trail figured furs and embroidered hems.
translations.idiomatic: They blush at hemp robes yet chase ambition with silken pride."

sentences.zh: 且能約其躬，則儋石之畜以豐；

translations.literal: Moreover if one can restrain the self, then a few dan of stores counts as abundance;
translations.idiomatic: Master restraint and even modest savings feel lavish;

sentences.zh: 苟肆其欲，則海陵之積不足；

translations.literal: if one indulges desire, then even Hailing's hoard is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: indulge appetite and even oceanic granaries cannot satisfy.

sentences.zh: 存道德者，則匹夫之身可榮；

translations.literal: Those who preserve virtue may honor a commoner's person;
translations.idiomatic: Cherish moral principle and a commoner shines with dignity;

sentences.zh: 忘大倫者，則萬乘之主猶辱。

translations.literal: those who forget great human relations remain disgraced though lords of ten thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: betray cardinal ethics and even an emperor wears shame.

sentences.zh: 將研六籍以訓世，守寂泊以鎮俗，偶鄭老於海隅，匹嚴叟於僻蜀。

translations.literal: I intend to study the Six Classics to instruct the age, keep quiet emptiness to steady custom, pair Old Zheng by the sea's edge, match Old Yan in remote Shu.
translations.idiomatic: I will mine the Six Classics to instruct the world, anchor myself in tranquil simplicity to steady manners, stand beside Old Zheng on the coast and Old Yan in western Shu."

sentences.zh: 且世乙太虛為輿，玄爐為肆，神游莫競之林，心存無營之室，榮利不擾其覺，殷憂不幹其寐，捐誇者之所貪，收躁務之所棄，雉聖籍之荒蕪，總群言之一至。

translations.literal: Moreover I take the Grand Void as my carriage and the dark furnace as my booth; my spirit roams groves where none compete and my mind halls in chambers without striving—glory and profit do not disturb waking, deep sorrow does not disrupt sleep; I abandon what boasters crave and gather what frantic ambition discards; I till the neglected garden of sages' texts and fuse myriad voices into single insight.
translations.idiomatic: I ride the vast empyrean as cart and the mysterious forge as shop—my soul wanders trackless woods while my heart nests in rooms free of schemes; profit cannot wake me from calm nor grief break my rest; I renounce what pretenders chase and reclaim what hustlers abandon; I weed overgrown classics and distill every doctrine to its essence."

sentences.zh: 全素履於丘園，背纓緌而長逸，請子課吾業於千載，無聽吾言於今日也。」

translations.literal: I preserve plain tread in hill gardens, cast aside official tassels for lasting ease—please judge my vocation across a thousand ages, not merely heed my words today."
translations.idiomatic: I keep unsullied footsteps in orchards and hills, turning my back on court ribbons for enduring leisure—evaluate my lifework in posterity, not just my speech this afternoon."

sentences.zh: 張華見而奇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua read it and deemed it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua saw the piece he marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 石鑒卒，王戎乃辟璆。

translations.literal: When Shi Jian died, Wang Rong finally summoned Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Jian passed away, Wang Rong at last offered Qiu a post.

sentences.zh: 華召晳為掾，又為司空、下邳王晃所辟。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua summoned Xi as an aide; he was also recruited by the Minister of Works, Prince Huang of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua invited Xi to serve as clerk, and the Minister of Works, Prince Huang of Xiapi, likewise recruited him.

sentences.zh: 華為司空，復以為賊曹屬。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua became Minister of Works, he again appointed him as an aide in the Bandits Section.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Hua rose to Minister of Works, he reassigned Xi to the Bandits Bureau as clerk.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣農，晳上議曰：轉佐著作郎，撰《晉書·帝紀》、十《志》，遷轉博士，著作如故。

translations.literal: At that time wishing to expand agriculture, Xi submitted a memorial saying: He was transferred to Assistant Editorial Director, compiled the Jinshu Basic Annals and the Ten Treatises, was promoted in turn to Erudite, and continued in his editorial duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: The clause begins with expanding agriculture, then jumps abruptly to Shu Xi’s promotions—as if two unrelated strands were fused in copying. Read sequentially he served as assistant editorial director, helped compile the Jin annals and ten treatises, rose to academic erudite, and kept his editorial duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，，汲郡人不准盜發魏襄王墓，或言安釐王塚，得竹書數十車。

translations.literal: Formerly, a man of Ji Commandery named Bu Zhun broke open the tomb of King Xiang of Wei—some say it was the mound of King An of Li—and obtained bamboo documents filling dozens of carts.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, Bu Zhun of Ji Commandery looted the burial mound of King Xiang of Wei—or, some claimed, of King An of Li—and hauled out bamboo slips by the cartload.

sentences.zh: 其《紀年》十三篇，記夏以來至周幽王為犬戎所滅，以事接之，三家分，仍述魏事至安釐王之二十年。

translations.literal: Its Bamboo Annals in thirteen sections records events from Xia down to King You of Zhou’s destruction by the Quanrong; it connects the narrative to subsequent events, through the tripartite partition of Jin, and continues to relate Wei affairs down to the twentieth year of King An of Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Bamboo Annals, thirteen scrolls, runs from the Xia age to King You’s fall to the Quanrong; it picks up the thread through the three houses’ partition of Jin and carries Wei’s story to the twentieth year of King An’s reign.

sentences.zh: 蓋魏國之史書，大略與《春秋》皆多相應。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, this Wei state history largely corresponds with the Spring and Autumn Annals in many particulars.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly, Wei’s chronicle and the Spring and Autumn Annals align on many points.

sentences.zh: 其中經傳大異，則雲夏年多殷；

translations.literal: Where its classics and commentaries diverge greatly, it claims the Xia reign-years exceeded those of Yin;
translations.idiomatic: Where text and gloss part company sharply, it asserts Xia’s calendar ran longer than Shang’s;

sentences.zh: 益幹啟位，啟殺之；

translations.literal: Yi seized Qi’s throne; Qi killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrested the throne from Qi; Qi slew him;

sentences.zh: 太甲殺伊尹；

translations.literal: Tai Jia killed Yi Yin;
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia put Yi Yin to death;

sentences.zh: 文丁殺季曆；

translations.literal: Wen Ding killed Ji Li;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen Ding executed Ji Li;

sentences.zh: 自周受命，至穆王百年，非穆王壽百歲也；

translations.literal: From Zhou receiving the Mandate down to King Mu was one hundred years—it does not mean King Mu lived one hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: From Zhou’s receipt of Heaven’s charge to King Mu spans a century—not that Mu himself lived a hundred years;

sentences.zh: 幽王既亡，有共伯和者攝行天子事，非二相共和也。

translations.literal: After King You perished, a certain Elder He of Gong acted as regent in the Son of Heaven’s affairs—it was not the joint regime of two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When King You fell, Elder He of Gong held the royal interim—not the dual stewardship miscalled ‘Joint Harmony.’

sentences.zh: 其《易經》二篇，與《周易》上下經同。

translations.literal: Its Changes Classic in two sections matches the Zhouyi upper and lower classics.
translations.idiomatic: Its two-scroll Changes parallels the Zhouyi’s upper and lower wings.

sentences.zh: 《易繇陰陽卦》二篇，與《周易》略同，《繇辭》則異。

translations.literal: Its Yi Yaoyin Yang Hexagrams in two sections broadly resemble the Zhouyi, but the Yaoci texts differ.
translations.idiomatic: The pair titled Yi Yaoyin Yang Hexagrams roughly tracks the Zhouyi while its line texts diverge.

sentences.zh: 《卦下易經》一篇，似《說卦》而異。

translations.literal: Its Hexagram-subordinate Changes Classic in one piece resembles the Shuogua but is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The piece called Hexagram-subordinate Changes looks like the Shuogua yet departs from it.

sentences.zh: 《公孫段》二篇，公孫段與邵陟論《易》。

translations.literal: Its Gong Sun Duan in two sections: Gong Sun Duan disputing the Changes with Shao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls of Gong Sun Duan record his debate on the Changes with Shao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 《國語》三篇，言楚、晉事。

translations.literal: Its Discourses of the States in three sections speaks of Chu and Jin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three scrolls of Discourses of the States treat Chu and Jin.

sentences.zh: 《名》三篇，似《禮記》，又似《爾雅》《論語》。

translations.literal: Its Names in three sections resembles the Record of Rites, and also resembles the Erya and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Three scrolls titled Names echo the Record of Rites and recall the Erya and Analects.

sentences.zh: 《師春》一篇，書《左傳》諸卜筮，「師春」似是造書者姓名也。

translations.literal: Its Shi Chun in one piece records the divinations from the Zuo Tradition; ‘Shi Chun’ seems to be the compiler’s name.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chun, one scroll, collects Zuo-style oracle readings; the title likely memorializes its author.

sentences.zh: 《瑣語》十一篇，諸國卜夢妖怪相書也。

translations.literal: Its Suoyu in eleven sections is a composite of states’ dream omens, prodigies, and physiognomy writings.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven scrolls of Suoyu gather omens, dreams, and fate lore from many lands.

sentences.zh: 《梁丘藏》一篇，先敘魏之世數，次言丘藏金玉事。

translations.literal: Its Liangqiu Zang in one piece first narrates Wei’s reign-counts, then speaks of hill-store gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqiu Zang opens with Wei’s generations, then turns to treasure buried in the mound.

sentences.zh: 《繳書》二篇，論弋射法。

translations.literal: Its Jiaoshu in two sections discusses archery by trailing cord.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls of Jiaoshu expound the trailing-line hunt.

sentences.zh: 《生封》一篇，帝王所封。

translations.literal: Its Sheng Feng in one piece lists what emperors enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Feng catalogs imperial enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 《大曆》二篇，鄒子談天類也。

translations.literal: Its Great Calendar in two sections belongs with Master Zou’s talks on heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls of Great Calendar belong to the astronomizing school of Zou Yan.

sentences.zh: 《穆天子傳》五篇，言周穆王遊行四海，見帝台、西王母。

translations.literal: Its Mu Tianzi Zhuan in five sections describes King Mu of Zhou roaming the four seas, visiting the Terrace of the Emperor and the Queen Mother of the West.
translations.idiomatic: Five scrolls of Mu Tianzi Zhuan follow King Mu across the seas to the Emperor’s terrace and Xiwangmu’s realm.

sentences.zh: 《圖詩》一篇，畫贊之屬也。

translations.literal: Its Tu Shi in one piece belongs to the genre of painted encomia.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Shi is of the picture-caption kind.

sentences.zh: 又雜書十九篇：《周食田法》，《周書》，《論楚事》，《周穆王美人盛姬死事》。

translations.literal: Further sundry writings nineteen pieces: Zhou Field-allotment Law, Zhou Documents, On Chu Affairs, The Death of King Mu of Zhou’s Beauty Sheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen miscellanies follow—field law, Zhou documents, Chu affairs, and the death of King Mu’s favorite Sheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 大凡七十五篇，七篇簡書折壞，不識名題。

translations.literal: Altogether seventy-five pieces; seven bamboo bundles were broken and illegible, their titles unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five titles in all; seven slip-bundles snapped beyond reading, names lost.

sentences.zh: 塚中又得銅劍一枚，長二尺五寸。

translations.literal: From the tomb also came one bronze sword, two feet five inches long.
translations.idiomatic: They also pulled a bronze blade two feet five inches from the mound.

sentences.zh: 漆書皆科斗字。

translations.literal: The lacquer writing was all in tadpole script.
translations.idiomatic: Every character was lacquered tadpole script.

sentences.zh: 初發塚者燒策照取寶物，及官收之，多燼簡斷劄，文既殘缺，不復詮次。

translations.literal: At first the grave-openers burned slips for light to seize valuables; when officials recovered them, many were charred, snapped, or shredded—the text was ruined and could no longer be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Looters torched bamboo for light; when the state salvaged the haul, char and breaks left the text unsalvageable for collation.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其書付秘書校綴次第，尋考指歸，而以今文寫之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu handed the cache to the Palace Library to stitch sequence and repair breaks, trace intended meaning, and transcribe it into modern script.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted the bundle to the secretariat for restoration, sense-finding, and conversion into current graphs.

sentences.zh: 晳在著作，得觀竹書，隨疑分釋，皆有義證。

translations.literal: While Xi held his editorial post he could inspect the bamboo texts; wherever doubt arose he analyzed and glossed, each point grounded in evidence.
translations.idiomatic: As editor, Xi studied the slips firsthand, resolving doubts with argued readings.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問摯虞三日曲水之義，虞對曰：「漢章帝時，平原徐肇以三月初生三女，至三日俱亡，村人以為怪，乃招攜之水濱洗祓，遂因水以泛觴，其義起此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Zhi Yu the meaning of the third-day winding-water rite; Yu replied: ‘In Zhang of Han’s reign, Xu Zhao of Pingyuan bore three daughters on the third of the third month; all three died that day; the villagers thought it uncanny and led families to the stream to wash and exorcise; hence floating cups on the water—the custom began thus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quizzed Zhi Yu on ‘winding water’ on day three. Yu’s tale: during Han Zhangdi, Xu Zhao of Pingyuan’s triple birth on the double-third ended in triple death; villagers drew kin to the bank for ablution, then cups rode the current—that, he said, was the origin.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「必如所談，便非好事。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor said: ‘If it truly began so, it was no happy thing.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered: If your story is true, the custom began in grief, not joy.

sentences.zh: 」晳進曰：「虞小生，不足以知，臣請言之。

translations.literal: ’ Xi stepped forward: ‘Yu is young and cannot know; allow your servant to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xi interjected: The lad lacks breadth—I will explain.

sentences.zh: 昔周公成洛邑，因流水以泛酒，故逸詩云『羽觴隨波』。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou completed Luoyi and floated wine along the flowing water; thus lost Odes lines say “feather goblets drift with the waves.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou finished Luoyi he let cups ride the current—hence the stray verse, ‘feathered cups on the wave.’

sentences.zh: 又秦昭王以三日置酒河曲，見金人奉水心之劍，曰：『令君制有西夏。

translations.literal: Again King Zhao of Qin on the third day set wine at the river’s bend and saw a golden man present a sword from the water’s heart, saying: ‘May my lord rule Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Qin feasted at the river bend on day three and saw a golden figure offer a sword from midstream: ‘You shall master Western Xia.’

sentences.zh: 』乃霸諸侯，因此立為曲水。

translations.literal: ’ Then he lorded it over the feudatories; on that account he established winding water.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he rose above the lords—and founded the winding-water gathering.

sentences.zh: 二漢相緣，皆為盛集。

translations.literal: The two Han dynasties carried it on in succession; each held splendid assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Both Han courts continued it as grand festivals.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，賜晳金五十斤。

translations.literal: ’ The emperor was greatly pleased and granted Xi fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign delighted and weighed out fifty jin of gold for Xi.

sentences.zh: 時有人于嵩高山下得竹簡一枚，上兩行科斗書，傳以相示，莫有知者。

translations.literal: At that time someone found beneath Song Mountain a single bamboo slip with two lines of tadpole script; it was passed hand to hand and none could read it.
translations.idiomatic: Then a lone slip surfaced under Songshan—two lines nobody could decipher.

sentences.zh: 司空張華以問晳，晳曰：「此漢明帝顯節陵中策文也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua showed it to Xi; Xi said: ‘This is the cedar-text from Emperor Ming’s Xianjie mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua brought it to Xi, who declared it the cedar-plaque wording from Mingdi’s Xianjie tomb.

sentences.zh: 」檢驗果然，時人伏其博識。

translations.literal: ’ Inspection proved him right; people of the time admired his vast learning.
translations.idiomatic: Verification bore him out; contemporaries bowed to his erudition.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫為相國，請為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao of Zhao serving as Chancellor of State invited Xi to be his secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lun of Zhao held the chancellorship he asked Xi to join his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晳辭疾罷歸，教授門徒。

translations.literal: Xi pleaded illness, resigned, and returned home to teach disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Xi pleaded sickness, withdrew, and taught students.

sentences.zh: 年四十卒，元城市裏為之廢業，門生故人立碑墓側。

translations.literal: He died at forty; Yuanshi ward silenced its trades for him; pupils and old friends raised a stele beside his grave.
translations.idiomatic: He fell at forty; Yuan district stilled its markets; disciples and friends carved stone at his mound.

sentences.zh: 晳才學博通，所著《三魏人士傳》，《七代通記》、《晉書·紀》、《志》，遇亂亡失。

translations.literal: Xi’s talents ranged wide; his Three Wei Worthies Biography, Seven Dynasties Comprehensive Record, Jinshu Annals and Treatises—all were lost in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His oeuvre—Three Wei Worthies, Seven Dynasties overview, Jin annals and treatises—vanished in the wars.

sentences.zh: 其《五經通論》、《發蒙記》、《補亡詩》、文集數十篇，行於世雲。

translations.literal: His Five Classics Comprehensive Discussion, Primers Record, Supplementary Lost Odes, and collected writings in several tens of pieces circulated in the world, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: What survived reputedly included his Five Classics synthesis, Primers, patched ‘lost’ odes, and dozens of collected pieces.

sentences.zh: 王接

translations.literal: Wang Jie
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie

sentences.zh: 王接，字祖遊，河東猗氏人，漢京兆尹尊十世孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, courtesy Zuyou, was a man of Yishi in Hedong, tenth-generation descendant of Han’s Metropolitan Governor Wang Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, styled Zuyou, from Yishi in Hedong—the tenth generation down from Wang Zun, Han’s capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 父蔚，世修儒史之學。

translations.literal: His father Wei practiced Confucian and historical scholarship for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei sustained generations of classical and historical learning.

sentences.zh: 魏中領軍曹羲作《至公論》，蔚善之，而著《至機論》，辭義甚美。

translations.literal: Wei Commandant-in-Chief Cao Xi wrote On Utmost Impartiality; Wei praised it and composed On Utmost Pivot; its phrasing was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Army commander Cao Xi’s Utmost Impartiality impressed Wei, who answered with Utmost Pivot—language of rare polish.

sentences.zh: 官至夏陽侯相。

translations.literal: His office reached Marquis of Xiayang’s chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to magistrate for the Marquis of Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 接幼喪父，哀毀過禮，鄉親皆歎曰：「王氏有子哉！

translations.literal: Jie lost his father while young; his grief exceeded ritual measure; neighbors sighed: ‘The Wangs have a true son!
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Jie mourned past the rites; neighbors murmured, The Wang line has an heir.

sentences.zh: 」渤海劉原為河東太守，好奇，以旌才為務。

translations.literal: ’ Liu Yuan of Bohai, serving as Hedong governor, loved the unusual and made displaying talent his task.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan of Bohai, as Hedong governor, courted wonder and hunted talent.

sentences.zh: 同郡馮收試經為郎，七十餘，薦接于原曰：「夫驊騮不總轡，則非造父之肆；

translations.literal: Feng Shou of the same commandery passed the classics examination and became a gentleman; past seventy he recommended Jie to Yuan, saying: ‘If fine steeds wear no gathered reins, they are not in Zaofu’s stable;
translations.idiomatic: Co-provincial Feng Shou, a classics-tested gentleman past seventy, urged Yuan: ‘Unbitted bays never reach Zaofu’s yard;

sentences.zh: 明月不流光，則非隋侯之掌。

translations.literal: if the bright moon sheds no flowing light, it is not in Marquis Sui’s palm.
translations.idiomatic: Moonlight unfelt never rests in Sui Hou’s hand.’

sentences.zh: 伏惟明府苞黃中之德，耀重離之明，求賢與能，小無遺錯，是以鄙老思獻所知。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Honor embraces virtue at the yellow center and shines with doubled li’s clarity; you seek worth and ability without overlooking the smallest talent—therefore this rustic elder wishes to offer what he knows.
translations.idiomatic: He trusts Your Honor’s centered virtue and luminous clarity; you miss no gifted soul—so this old man offers a name.

sentences.zh: 竊見處士王接，岐嶷俊異，十三而孤，居喪盡禮，學過目而知，義觸類而長，斯玉鉉之妙味，經世之徽猷也。

translations.literal: Privately I have observed the recluse Wang Jie: precocious and outstanding, orphaned at thirteen, observing mourning with full propriety; learning—once seen, understood; principles—touching one class, he lengthened all—this is the subtle savor of the jade tripods’ handle, the fine plan that orders the age.
translations.idiomatic: The witness: young Jie, brilliant, bereaved at thirteen yet ritually perfect—reads once and grasps, infers wide—the savor of the sacred tripods, policy for an era.

sentences.zh: 不患玄黎之不啟，竊樂春英之及時。

translations.literal: I do not worry that black grain will not open; I privately rejoice that spring blossoms arrive in season.
translations.idiomatic: I do not fret that night grain fails to sprout—I rejoice spring blooms on time.

sentences.zh: 」原即禮命，接不受。

translations.literal: ’ Yuan immediately sent ritual summons; Jie would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan dispatched formal invitation; Jie declined.

sentences.zh: 原乃呼見曰：「君欲慕肥遁之高邪？

translations.literal: Yuan then called him in and said: ‘Do you wish to emulate the lofty reclusion of Fei?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan summoned him: Do you chase Fei’s lofty withdrawal?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「接薄祜，少孤而無兄弟，母老疾篤，故無心為吏。

translations.literal: ’ He replied: ‘Jie has thin fortune, was orphaned young without brothers, and his mother is aged and gravely ill—therefore he has no heart for office.
translations.idiomatic: Jie answered: Little blessing left me fatherless and brotherless with a dying mother—office holds no lure.

sentences.zh: 」及母終，柴毀骨立，居墓次積年，備覽眾書，多出異義。

translations.literal: ’ When his mother died, he wasted to bones by grief; he dwelt by the tomb for years, exhaustively reading many books and producing many divergent interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: When she passed he withered beside her mound for years, reading widely and arguing fresh glosses.

sentences.zh: 性簡率，不修俗操，鄉里大族多不能善之，唯裴頠雅知焉。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and direct; he cultivated no fashionable conduct; great local clans mostly could not warm to him—only Pei Yi truly understood him.
translations.idiomatic: Plain-spoken, indifferent to fashion, grand families spurned him—only Pei Yi saw his worth.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守柳澹、散騎侍郎裴遐、尚書僕射鄧攸皆與接友善。

translations.literal: Pingyang governor Liu Dan, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Xia, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Deng You were all friendly with Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Dan of Pingyang, attendant Pei Xia, and minister Deng You counted him friend.

sentences.zh: 後為郡主簿，迎太守溫宇，宇奇之，轉功曹史。

translations.literal: Later he became county clerk for documentation; welcoming Governor Wen Yu, Yu marveled at him and transferred him to merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as county registrar, impressed incoming Governor Wen Yu, and became merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 州辟部平陽從事。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Pingyang adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: The province appointed him Pingyang staff officer.

sentences.zh: 時泰山羊亮為平陽太守，薦之于司隸校尉王堪，出補都官從事。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Liang of Taishan was Pingyang governor; he recommended Jie to Metropolitan Governor Wang Kan, who appointed him assistant for capital affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan’s Yang Liang, then Pingyang governor, pushed Jie to Wang Kan, who gave him a capital-affairs post.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，舉秀才。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning he was nominated cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongning’s opening year he earned the ‘cultivated talent’ nomination.

sentences.zh: 友人滎陽潘滔遺接書曰：「摯虞、卞玄仁並謂足下應和鼎味，可無以應秀才行。

translations.literal: His friend Pan Tao of Xingyang sent Jie a letter: ‘Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren both say you should harmonize the tripods’ savor—can you ignore the cultivated-talent summons?
translations.idiomatic: Friend Pan Tao wrote: Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren say you belong at the cauldron—will you spurn nomination?

sentences.zh: 」接報書曰：「今世道交喪，將遂剝亂，而識智之士鉗口韜筆，禍敗日深，如火之燎原，其可救乎？

translations.literal: ’ Jie answered: ‘In this age the Way lies ruined in mutual ruin; stripping and chaos will follow; wise men seal lips and sheathe brushes; calamity deepens daily like fire spreading across the plain—can it be saved?
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied: The age rots toward collapse; the wise shut mouth and pen while disaster spreads like flame—who can stem it?

sentences.zh: 非榮斯行，欲極陳所見，冀有覺悟耳。

translations.literal: It is not glory that drives this journey; I wish only to lay out what I see, hoping for awakening.
translations.idiomatic: Not for glory—I mean to speak plain truth and wake someone.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，三王義舉，惠帝復阼，以國有大慶，天下秀孝一皆不試，接以為恨。

translations.literal: ’ That year the three princes raised the righteous host; Emperor Hui resumed the throne; because the state had great celebration, all nominated ‘cultivated’ and ‘filial’ candidates nationwide went untested—Jie considered it a regret.
translations.idiomatic: That year the three princes revolted; Hui returned; national jubilee waived exams for every nominee—Jie mourned the lost trial.

sentences.zh: 除中郎，補征虜將軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the palace and supplemented Attendant General Who Subdues Captives’ marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He took gentleman rank and filled Subduing Captives general’s staff marshal.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，侍中嵇紹為亂兵所害，接議曰：「夫謀人之軍，軍敗則死之；

translations.literal: In the Battle of Dangyin, Palace Attendant Ji Shao was killed by mutinous troops; Jie argued: ‘One who plots another’s army—when the army fails, dies for it;
translations.idiomatic: At Dangyin, mutineers slew Ji Shao; Jie argued: Plot another’s host—fail and die with it;

sentences.zh: 謀人之國，國危則亡之，古之道也。

translations.literal: one who plots another’s state—when the state is imperiled, perishes for it: the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: plot another’s realm—peril it and perish: antiquity’s rule.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，百官奔北，唯嵇紹守職以遇不道，可謂臣矣，又可稱痛矣。

translations.literal: In the Dangyin affair the hundred officials fled north; only Ji Shao held his post against lawlessness—he may be called a minister, and may be called heartbreaking.
translations.idiomatic: While courtiers ran, Shao stood his ground against outrage—a minister and a wound.

sentences.zh: 今山東方欲大舉，宜明高節，以號令天下。

translations.literal: Now the eastern march plans a great campaign; it should proclaim lofty integrity to command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The east readies war—signal supreme fidelity to rally the world.

sentences.zh: 依《春秋》褒三累之義，加紹致命之賞，則遐邇向風，莫敢不肅矣。

translations.literal: Following the Spring and Autumn’s praise of threefold accumulation of merit, add to Shao the reward due one who gave his life—then far and near will turn like wind and none dare show disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Apply Spring and Autumn praise for triple merit; crown Shao’s martyr’s wage—then all quarters heed.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: ’ The court followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒欲遷駕長安，與關東乖異，以接成都王佐，難之，表轉臨汾公相國。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong wished to move the imperial carriage to Chang’an; discord with the eastern alliance—because Jie was Chengdu Prince’s aide he held it difficult and memorialized a transfer to county chancellor for the Prince of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian wanted the court in Chang’an, at odds with the east; Jie, Chengdu prince’s assistant, balked and was rotated to Linfen prince’s county chief.

sentences.zh: 及東海王越率諸候討顒，尚書令王堪統行台，上請接補尚書殿中郎，未至而卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: When Prince of the Eastern Seas Sima Yue led the lords against Yong, Masters of Writing chief Wang Kan headed the mobile directorate and memorialized Jie as Gentleman of the Palace Masters of Writing—before he arrived he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When Donghai Yue marched on Yong, minister Wang Kan’s field headquarters nominated Jie as palace secretary—he died en route at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 接學雖博通，特精《禮》《傳》。

translations.literal: Though Jie’s learning was vast, he especially excelled at the Rites and Traditions.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite broadly, he shone on Rites and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 常謂《左氏》辭義贍富，自是一家書，不主為經發。

translations.literal: He often said the Zuo language is rich in gloss and sense—its own book, not chiefly composed to open the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He held Zuo its own literary cosmos—not mainly a key to the classics.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》附經立傳，經所不書，傳不妄起，于文為儉，通經為長。

translations.literal: The Gongyang anchors gloss to classic; what the classic omits, gloss does not invent—literarily spare, for penetrating the classics it excels.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang ties commentary to text; silence in canon stays silence in gloss—lean prose, excellent for threading the classics.

sentences.zh: 任城何休訓釋甚詳，而黜周王魯，大體乖硋，且志通《公羊》而往往還為《公羊》疾病。

translations.literal: Rencheng He Xiu’s commentary is minute yet demotes Zhou and enthrones Lu—broadly skewed—and though intent on Gongyang he often becomes Gongyang’s ailment.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu of Rencheng glosses minutely yet demotes Zhou for Lu—warped—and his Gongyang zeal breeds Gongyang’s own sickness.

sentences.zh: 接乃更注《公羊春秋》，多有新義。

translations.literal: Jie therefore reannotated Gongyang’s Spring and Autumn, often with fresh senses.
translations.idiomatic: So Jie rewrote Gongyang with many new readings.

sentences.zh: 時秘書丞衛恆考正汲塚書，未訖而遭難。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Library Assistant Wei Heng was collating the Ji tomb texts but had not finished when disaster struck.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat aide Wei Heng edited the Ji cache unfinished when calamity hit.

sentences.zh: 佐著作郎束皙述而成之，事多證異義。

translations.literal: Assistant Editorial Director Shu Xi carried it to completion, many points verified with divergent readings.
translations.idiomatic: Editor Shu Xi finished the job, evidence often clashing.

sentences.zh: 時東萊太守陳留王庭堅難之，亦有證據。

translations.literal: At that time Chenliu Wang Tingjian, governor of Donglai, challenged it; he too had proofs.
translations.idiomatic: Donglai governor Wang Tingjian of Chenliu disputed him—with documentation.

sentences.zh: 皙又釋難，而庭堅已亡。

translations.literal: Xi answered the challenge, but Tingjian had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi rebutted after Tingjian died.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎潘滔謂接曰：「卿才學理議，足解二子之紛，可試論之。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Pan Tao told Jie: ‘Your talent and reason suffice to settle the two men’s quarrel—essay it.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao urged: Your learning can end their feud—write it out.

sentences.zh: 」接遂詳其得失。

translations.literal: ’ Jie then detailed their merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jie weighed both sides.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、謝衡皆博物多聞，咸以為允當。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu and Xie Heng were both broadly learned; both deemed it fair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Xie Heng, encyclopedic, called it just.

sentences.zh: 又撰《列女後傳》七十二人，雜論議、詩賦、碑頌、駁難十餘萬言，喪亂盡失。

translations.literal: He also compiled Later Biographies of Exemplary Women, seventy-two figures, mixed essays, rhapsodies, dirges, stele hymns, and polemics exceeding one hundred thousand graphs—all lost in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: He authored seventy-two Later Exemplary Women plus essays, fu, eulogy, stele, debate—over hundred thousand graphs—gone in war.

sentences.zh: 長子愆期，流寓江南，緣父本意，更注《公羊》，又集《列女後傳》云。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qianqi drifted south of the Yangzi; following his father’s intent he reannotated Gongyang and reassembled Later Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Qianqi fled south and, honoring his intent, re-glossed Gongyang and recollected the women’s sequel.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historical appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: 【Court historians’ verdict】

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：皇甫謐素履幽貞，閒居養疾，留情筆削，敦悅丘墳，軒冕未足為榮，貧賤不以為恥，確乎不拔，斯固有晉之高人者歟！

translations.literal: The historians say: Huangfu Mi walked a plain path in secluded integrity; dwelling retired he nursed illness, lavishing care on brush-cut ink, devoted to ancient learning—carriage-and-cap honor could not tempt him, poverty and low estate did not shame him—steadfastly unmoved: surely among Jin’s lofty recluses!
translations.idiomatic: The editors: Huangfu Mi kept plain virtue in quiet withdrawal—ink for illness, joy in tombs—unswayed by rank or poverty: a Jin-era recluse among recluses.

sentences.zh: 洎乎《篤終》立論，薄葬昭儉，既戒奢于季氏，亦無取于王孫，可謂達存亡之機矣。

translations.literal: When he framed ‘Earnest Endings,’ preaching thin burial and revealing thrift—warning extravagance like the Ji clan yet rejecting Prince Yang’s stance—he may be called one who grasped the hinge of life and death.
translations.idiomatic: His ‘Earnest Endings’ essay favors humble graves—scorning Ji excess yet avoiding Yang’s nihilism—seeing clear through mortality’s door.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、束皙等並詳覽載籍，多識舊章，奏議可觀，文詞雅贍，可謂博聞之士也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, Shu Xi and others together examined texts broadly and knew the old statutes well; their memorial discourses repay reading and their language is elegant and rich—they may be called men of wide learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Shu Xi among others mastered the archives and classical precedent; their counsel reads well and their prose glows—they rank among the truly learned.

sentences.zh: 或攝官延閣，裁成言事之書；

translations.literal: Some held provisional posts in the prolonging pavilion, trimming writings that present policy.
translations.idiomatic: Some staffed the imperial library on provisional assignment and shaped policy memorials.

sentences.zh: 或蒞政秩宗，參定禋郊之禮。

translations.literal: Some administered at the Minister of Rites, assisting to settle suburban sacrifice ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Others oversaw the ministry of rites and helped fix suburban offerings.

sentences.zh: 虞既厄於從理，皙乃年位不充，天之報施，何其爽也！

translations.literal: Yu already met obstruction in following principle; Xi then lacked years and rank—Heaven's repayment—how uneven!
translations.idiomatic: Yu suffered for holding fast to duty; Xi died before his talents ripened—how strangely Heaven rewards men.

sentences.zh: 王接才調秀出，見賞知音，惜其夭枉，未申驥足，嗟夫！

translations.literal: Wang Jie's talents stood brilliant; he won appreciation from those who understand—alas early death cut him short before stretching thoroughbred hoofs—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie's gifts dazzled connoisseurs, yet heaven clipped him before his stride—what waste.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：士安好逸，棲心蓬蓽。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Shi'an loved ease and lodged his heart in brushwood gates.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Huangfu Mi sought quiet and dwelt among humble lanes.

sentences.zh: 屬意文雅，忘懷榮秩。

translations.literal: He fixed intent on polished letters and forgot glory of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished care on literature and ignored titles.

sentences.zh: 遺制可稱，養生乖術。

translations.literal: His testament writings merit praise; nurturing life missed true method.
translations.idiomatic: His burial essays deserve praise; Cold Food elixirs betrayed his health.

sentences.zh: 摯虞博聞，廣微絕群。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu learned broadly; Guangwei surpassed the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu ranged wide; Shu Guangwei stood apart.

sentences.zh: 財成禮度，刊緝遺文。

translations.literal: They completed ritual norms and carved up remnant texts.
translations.idiomatic: They shaped ritual law and edited stray manuscripts.

sentences.zh: 魏篇式序，漢冊斯分。

translations.literal: Wei bamboo tales gained order; Han silk registers stood sorted.
translations.idiomatic: Archives from Wei gained sequence; Han slips found their place.

sentences.zh: 祖遊後出，亦播清芬。

translations.literal: Zuyou came later—yet spreads pure fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuyou rose afterward—and still perfumes later ages.
